BIOL385L
Microbiology Lab
1
Microbiology laboratory is a two hours a week laboratory course with
experiments in microbial culture, staining techniques, disinfection, and
sterilization. Isolation of bacteria from mixed cultures. Use various
metabolic reactions in the identification and classification of organisms.
BIOL385
Microbiology
3
This course covers principles of microbiology with emphasizing on the
diversity and structural characteristics of microorganisms, impact of
microbes on everyday life and the role of microbes in the host-pathogen
interactions. Moreover, in this course, you will be introduced to the
world of microbiology in terms of isolation, identification and
classification. Also, you will have the chance to discover examples of
different groups and species of microorganisms that have direct impact
on human health, mechanism of causing diseases and the beneficial
effects on the biotechnology sector as applications in the food industry.
BIOL360L
Human Physiology
& Anatomy Lab
1
This lab deals with the structure of the human body. It includes the
study of tissues, skeletal, muscular, nervous, and cardiovascular
systems. It is presented using microscopic slides, human skeletal
models, anatomical models, drawings, and dissections. 
BIOL360
Human Physiology
& Anatomy
4
This course is designed to teach students human physiology and
anatomy. Physiology is the study of the process or function of living
things. The major goals of physiology are to understand the response of
the body to stimuli and understand how the body maintains conditions
within homeostasis in various environmental conditions. The study of
physiology consists of many different levels including cell physiology,
organ physiology and systemic physiology. Students will be exposed to
all of these levels starting at the cellular level and eventually moving up
to the system level. Physiology and anatomy are closely related
subjects. Anatomy is the scientific discipline that investigates body
structures. Often to fully appreciate the physiology of a given system it
is necessary to first examine its anatomy. A true understanding and
appreciation of physiology can only occur if structure and function are
concurrently learned.
BIOL200L
General Biology I
Lab
1
General Biology I lab introduces students to basic techniques and safety
practices in the laboratory;
 
reinforcing the concepts learned in General
Biology I lecture. It provides hands-on experience of some of the
concepts discussed in the latter course.
BIOL200
General Biology I
3
This course aims to familiarize the student with the organization and
classification of living systems. The covered topics include mainly the
cell structure and function, cell division, cell biochemistry, cellular
respiration, DNA structure and protein function, as well as animal
development and classification. This course has a separate one credit-
laboratory component.
 
BIOC310
Medical
Biochemistry
4
The study of human biochemistry describes how the body works, and
provides a basis for understanding what can, and often does, go wrong.
From a physician's point of view, biochemistry provides not only a
description of 
how the system works
, but also a foundation for
understanding how to improve its operation through appropriate
nutrition, exercise, preventive medicine, 
how to diagnose problems
and, where possible, 
how to remedy them. 
Current therapies include
recombinant proteins, such as human insulin or erythropoietin
synthesized by bacteria, and future therapies will include genetic
engineering, involving gene rather than organ transplants. To
understand how the human body works, and the basis of the therapies
for its maintenance and healing, it is essential to understand not only
the chemistry of the reactions, but also the functional interactions
between metabolic pathways, organs, and tissues. This, in a broad
sense, is the realm of physiologic biochemistry.

3
This course builds upon the skills acquired in pre-requisite courses mainly
ENGL 151 to further develop students’ critical thinking and academic
writing competencies. Students will read and respond to a variety of texts
from different disciplines and produce a research paper using analytical
and critical skills in response to texts.
ENGL251
Communication
Skills
3
Workplace Occupational Writing is an advanced interdisciplinary writing
course emphasizing workplace and technical communication and editing
appropriate to diverse professions. It incorporates practice and study of
selected types of discourse employed in professional writing situations,
preparing students for different systems of writing in their professional
lives. Examples from the writing of workplace professionals are analyzed
and used as models to demonstrate the transition from academic to
professional writing.

This course explores brain structure and functions, including
thinking/decision making, and cognition. It examines personality

EDUC220
Principles of
Education
3
Teaching is both a creative and structured endeavor that involves
motivating, guiding, and supporting learners. This course provides a
foundational introduction to the core principles and practices of effective
teaching, setting the stage for a lifelong journey in education. Through a
combination of interactive lectures, case-based discussions, and practical
activities, students will explore essential topics such as the qualities of
effective educators, student diversity, curriculum planning, classroom
management, and the integration of educational technology. Learners will
gain the skills necessary to design dynamic, inclusive, and tech-enhanced
learning environments. They will also engage with authentic teaching
scenarios, collaborate with peers on educational tasks, and reflect on their
evolving roles as educators. By the end of the course, students will have a
clear understanding of the educatorâs impact, be equipped with evidence-
based teaching strategies, and foster a commitment to ongoing professional
development. This course empowers future educators with the knowledge,
confidence, and mindset needed to positively influence learners and
educational communities.
EDUC222
Basics of
Educational
Psychology
3
Unlocking How We Learn: How do our thinking, social interactions, values,
and actions shape how students learn and grow__ This course dives into the
core ideas of educational psychology, helping students understand how
learners develop. By grasping these key areas, students will learn to create
lively lessons and implement effective classroom management strategies.
Throughout this course, students will explore the basic ideas and important
theories about how people develop, including their thinking, social lives,
moral understanding, and behaviors. The approach emphasizes seeing the
whole picture, encouraging students to use what they learn in real
classrooms. Through interesting talks, discussions, and hands-on activities,
students will gain the tools and knowledge needed to support students'
growth at every stage. By looking at both the theories and how they work in
practice, students will see how different teaching methods affect learning
outcomes. This course aims to equip future educators with the skills to
enhance learning across diverse educational settings, fostering both student
growth and their own professional journey.
EDUC251
Development of
Children and
Adolescents
3
Ever wondered how a tiny baby transforms into a complex teenager__ This
course takes students on a fascinating journey through the crucial stages of
child development, exploring the major theories and cutting-edge research
from the very beginning of life all the way to the start of formal schooling. It
will delve into the powerful forces that shape young lives, including the
dynamics within families, the impact of school settings, and the influence of
socioeconomic factors. Ultimately, this course aims to give students a solid
grasp of the key ideas and areas in childhood and adolescent development,
along with effective teaching approaches that truly support the well-being of
young learners.
EDUC252
Psychology of
Learning
3
How do we gain insight into the psychological mechanisms that drive
learning, and how can we leverage this understanding to improve
educational practices__ This course delves into foundational theories of
learning and cognitive processes, with particular emphasis on key concepts
such as memory, motivation, metacognition, and self-regulation. Through a
range of interactive and applied learning experiencesâincluding lesson
planning, case analyses, and collaborative dialogueâstudents will translate
theoretical knowledge into practical strategies for addressing real-world
educational challenges. By the end of the course, students will be equipped
to design effective learning environments, selec_t and implement
appropriate instructional techniques, and correct common misconceptions,
all while nurturing both critical and creative thinking. Ultimately, the course
prepares students to cultivate learner-centered classrooms that support deep
and lasting knowledge acquisition.
EDUC253
Technology
Integration in
Education
3
How can educators thoughtfully incorporate technology to boost student
achievement and engagement__ This course delves into the evolving role of
technology in the classroom, focusing on key themes like technology-
enhanced instruction, digital tools for differentiated learning, and the latest
innovations in educational tech. Through experiential learning, collaborative
projects, and case-based analysis, students will connect theory to practice by
integrating digital tools into authentic educational contexts. By the end of
the course, learners will be equipped to choose and implement appropriate
technologies across diverse educational settings, and design learner-
centered, tech-infused lessons that foster deep engagement and academic
success.
EDUC254
Basics of
Assessment &
Evaluation
3
Assessment of Learning offers a comprehensive exploration of both the
theoretical frameworks and research-based practices that inform effective
assessment in educational settings. Designed for future educators, the
course develops the competencies necessary to design, implement, and
evaluate a variety of assessment strategies that enhance teaching and
learning while promoting equity and inclusion. Grounded in contemporary
theories of learning and supported by empirical studies, this course
examines key principles of educational measurement, including validity,
reliability, fairness, and utility. Students will engage with a range of
assessment typesâformative, summative, diagnostic, and performance-
basedâalong with tools such as rubrics, standardized tests, and digital
assessment platforms. Emphasis is placed on aligning assessments with
instructional objectives and curriculum standards, using assessment data to
inform pedagogical decisions, and integrating culturally responsive and
inclusive practices. Through a combination of interactive lectures, case study
analysis, collaborative tasks, and practical workshops, students will gain
hands-on experience in constructing assessment tools, interpreting data, and
adapting assessment strategies to meet the needs of diverse learners. By the
end of the course, students will demonstrate not only a solid understanding
of foundational and contemporary theories of assessment but also the ability
to apply these principles to real-world classroom contexts in ways that
support student learning, foster motivation, and guide professional practice.
EDUC255
Fundamentals
of Curriculum
Design
3
This course provides an in-depth introduction to the core principles and
practices of curriculum design within a global educational context. Students
will engage with key topics including curriculum theory, educational
standards, and the evolving role of technology in shaping curriculum
development. Through a combination of interactive lectures, real-world case
studies, and practical activities, learners will explore how historical, cultural,
and societal factors influence curriculum and how it can be adapted to serve
diverse learning communities. By the end of the course, students will be able
to design inclusive, responsive curricula that address both local and
international educational needs. They will gain the tools to build curriculum
frameworks that encourage critical thinking, uphold educational equity, and
support continuous learning across varied educational settings.
EDUC320
Fundamentals
of Classroom
Management
3
Ever wonder how some classrooms just click, buzzing with focused energy
and a genuine love for learning__ The secret often lies in effective classroom
management â the very foundation upon which student potential is built
and a positive learning environment flourishes. This course delves into the
pivotal role of teachers as builders of such spaces, exploring how to cultivate
an atmosphere where students are not just present, but deeply engaged and
set up for success. It will uncover practical strategies for establishing a
proactive classroom where students naturally immerse themselves in tasks,
easily follow established rules and routines, and experience the focus that
comes from minimal distractions. Furthermore, this course equips future
educators with effective classroom management tools to help prepare them
for addressing disciplinary challenges and fostering a truly productive space
for learning. By the end of this course, participants will possess the tangible
skills to translate these strategies into real-world classroom settings,
ensuring a focused, supportive environment where every student can thrive.
EDUC322
Instructional
Methods
3
This course offers a comprehensive exploration of evidence-based
instructional methodologies designed to promote meaningful, inclusive, and
student-centered learning. Grounded in contemporary educational theories
and supported by empirical research, Methods of Teaching equips future
educators with the pedagogical knowledge and practical skills needed to
plan, implement, and assess effective instruction across diverse educational
settings. Participants will examine core components of instructional design,
including lesson planning aligned with learning outcomes, curriculum
standards, and learner diversity. Emphasis is placed on selecting and
adapting teaching strategies that foster active engagement, critical thinking,
and collaborative learning. Students will explore a range of instructional
modelsâsuch as direct instruction, inquiry-based learning, cooperative
learning, and differentiated instructionâand will develop competencies in
applying these models based on contextual and student-specific needs. The
course also investigates principles of classroom management, highlighting
strategies for creating safe, equitable, and productive learning
environments. Topics include managing classroom dynamics, responding to
student behavior, and cultivating positive teacher-student relationships
through proactive and restorative practices. Through lectures, case-based
learning, lesson simulations, and reflective practice, students will bridge
theory and practice, gaining the ability to make informed instructional
decisions grounded in research and real-world application. By the end of the
course, participants will be able to demonstrate a holistic understanding of
effective teaching practices and will possess a versatile instructional toolkit
to support student success in todayâs dynamic classrooms.
EDUC350
Basics of
Special
Education
3
Imagine a classroom where every student, regardless of their unique
learning needs, feels supported and empowered to thrive. This course dives
into the essential world of special education, exploring the core concepts,
legal frameworks, and practical strategies for effectively supporting diverse
learners within general education settings. Students will investigate the
wide spectrum of exceptionalities and their characteristics, from learning
disabilities to emotional and behavioral disorders, gaining critical insight
into their impact on learning and behavior. Through engaging discussions
and hands-on activities, the course will equip students with the knowledge to
implement inclusive practices and differentiate instruction effectively.
Students will learn to develop accessible lesson plans and utilize innovative
tools to cater to all students' needs. Furthermore, the course will provide a
thorough understanding of how to implement Individualized Education
Programs (IEPs) for students with special needs. By the end of the course,
students will possess a foundational understanding of special education,
enabling them to cultivate inclusive and supportive classroom environments.
They will be prepared to identify and address the diverse needs of students
with disabilities, employ effective teaching methodologies, and collaborate
with families and professionals to foster the success of every learner.

3
This course equips future educators with the foundational knowledge and
practical competencies essential for effective teaching at the elementary
level. Emphasizing both pedagogical development and reflective practice,
students will explore contemporary instructional strategies through
interactive case studies, experiential tasks, and peer collaboration. The
course highlights the value of observation, professional dialogue, and self-
reflection in shaping effective teaching habits and classroom dynamics.
Learners will analyze authentic teaching scenarios, design targeted lesson
plans, and participate in classroom simulations to deepen their
understanding of student-centered instruction. Focused on building
inclusive, engaging, and supportive learning environments, the course
prepares students to address the diverse academic and developmental
needs of young learners. By the end of the course, students will
demonstrate the ability to foster curiosity, collaboration, and critical
thinking in elementary classrooms.
EDUC326
Teaching
Learners at
Intermediate
Level
3
This course provides a focused exploration of the educational,
developmental, and emotional needs of learners in the intermediate years.
Centered on adolescent development, it equips future educators with the
tools to cultivate inclusive and responsive learning environments that
foster both academic and personal growth. Emphasis is placed on
relational pedagogies, student well-being, and collaborative teaching
practices that promote engagement and motivation. Through an
examination of curriculum design, instructional strategies, and assessment
methods tailored to this age group, students will gain a comprehensive
understanding of how to support learners during a critical stage of identity
formation and cognitive development. Through reflective inquiry, case
studies, and classroom-based simulations, students will emerge prepared to
implement differentiated and developmentally appropriate practices that
inspire critical thinking, resilience, and a lifelong love of learning in diverse
intermediate learners.
EDUC354
Understanding
Research in
Education
3
This course provides an introduction to the foundational sources and
methodologies of educational research. It equips students with the skills
needed to navigate the six key steps of the research process: identifying a
research problem, reviewing relevant literature, defining a purpose,
collecting data, analyzing and interpreting results, and presenting findings.
Additionally, the course covers fundamental concepts of descriptive
statistics.
EDUC422
Teaching
Practicum I
3
This course offers a foundational experience for future educators, serving
as a critical bridge between educational theory and real-world classroom
practice. Designed to cultivate reflective, adaptable, and student-centered
teaching approaches, the practicum emphasizes experiential learning
through 60 hours of structured classroom observation, tailored to the
specific focus of each education major. Throughout the course, students
will explore a variety of instructional methods, classroom management
strategies, and assessment tools, while engaging with constructivist, brain-
based, and metacognitive learning theories. Grounded in a philosophy of
inclusivity and lifelong learning, the course integrates reflective dialogue,
observation tools, evaluation rubrics, and the development of a professional
portfolio to track student growth. By the end of the practicum, students
will be able to critically evaluate teaching practices, contribute to inclusive
and effective learning environments, and clearly express their evolving
instructional philosophyâpreparing them to meet the diverse and ever-
changing demands of todayâs educational landscape.
EDUC452
Teaching
Practicum II
3
This course serves as a crucial follow-up to Teaching Practicum I,
advancing students' instructional competence and deepening their
practical teaching experience within authentic classroom environments.
Building on the foundational insights gained in the first practicum, this
course transitions students from primarily observational roles to active
teaching responsibilities. Emphasizing the integration of theory and
practice, the course enhances students' abilities in lesson planning,
differentiated instruction, classroom management, and learner
engagement, preparing them to address the varied needs of todayâs
diverse classrooms. Through immersive teaching placements, students will
observe, reflect, and take on teaching duties while applying pedagogical
theories to real-world contexts. Core topics include advanced instructional
strategies such as constructivist methods, active learning, and problem-
based learning. Students will also explore classroom differentiation,
assessment techniques, and inclusive teaching practices to meet the needs
of all learners. Throughout the course, students will refine their capacity to
design and deliver comprehensive, student-centered lesson plans that
promote critical thinking, creativity, and participation. Assignments include
microteaching, full-class teaching demonstrations, and the development of
a professional teaching portfolio. Continuous feedback from mentor
teachers and peers supports reflective practice and ongoing improvement.
By the end of the course, students will have confidently applied effective
teaching strategies in classroom settings, built a reflective portfolio
featuring lesson plans and teaching artifacts, and developed key
professional tools such as CVs and cover letters. This practicum equips
aspiring educators with the skills, confidence, and professional readiness
required for successful entry into the teaching profession.
ENGL221
English
Grammar in
Practice
3
Mastering the complexities of English grammar is key to becoming a clear
and effective communicator. This course delves into the structure and
function of modern English, helping you strengthen your communication
skills, refine your writing abilities, and develop critical thinking. A variety
of dynamic instructional approachesâsuch as lectures, assigned
readings, interactive tasks, group discussions, writing workshops, and
multimedia toolsâwill support your learning and provide opportunities to
apply grammatical knowledge in real-world contexts. You will engage with
grammar through listening, speaking, reading, and writing exercises that
encourage active use of language. These hands-on experiences are
designed to build a strong grammatical foundation, equipping you to
express ideas accurately and with confidence. Ongoing assessments and
individualized feedback will support steady improvement and focused
development. By the end of the course, you will have gained a
comprehensive understanding of modern English grammar and the ability
to communicate effectively across a range of situations.
ENGL320
Young Learners’
Literature
3
Young Learnersâ Literature, also known as Young Adult Literature (YAL),
introduces us to the tools for building an appreciation of reading and
finding meaningful engagement with literary texts. Exploring young adult
literature bridges personal reflections with collective classroom
discussions, transforming reading into both an individual and shared
experience. In this course, you will engage as both writers and readers,
offering interpretations shaped by reader-response theory. You will explore
various genres within young adult literature, and through close reading of
key texts, you will analyze themes and draw connections to real-world
contexts. The course also introduces foundational principles for teaching
YL literature and emphasizes hands-on instructional strategies designed to
create inclusive, activity-rich learning environments that address the needs
of diverse student populations.
ENGL321
English
Language
Curriculum
3
The English Language Curriculum centers on key principles and
methodologies for designing curricula tailored to English language
teaching. Specifically created for pre-service and novice ELT educators, the
course explores various contexts, processes, and strategies critical to
crafting effective language curricula. Rooted in a learner-focused and
reflective teaching approach, it highlights the significance of addressing
studentsâ diverse backgrounds and needs while bridging current
research and theoretical insights with practical teaching applications. The
course incorporates dynamic teaching methods, including interactive
lectures, collaborative projects, hands-on workshops, and reflective
exercises, fostering critical analysis, problem-solving, and the application
of theoretical knowledge to practical teaching situations. Instead of
traditional quizzes, evaluations focus on reflective activities, such as
textbook analysis based on the Lebanese national curriculum and
assessments of project-based curricula, aligning with the courseâs
teaching philosophy. This comprehensive program equips educators with
the expertise to develop, execute, and assess English language curricula
effectively, ensuring they can cater to varied student requirements and
support their own professional advancement.
EDUC351
Methods of
Teaching Oral
Communication
3
In a world where clear and effective communication is essential for success
in both academic and professional settings, the ability to teach oral
communication effectively has never been more important. This course
examines how oral communication can be taught successfully and which
instructional approaches best support the development of speaking and
listening abilities. It introduces key theories and pedagogical frameworks
related to oral communication, emphasizing practical techniques that
support pronunciation, listening comprehension, and spoken fluency.
Participants will explore essential concepts in oral communication
instruction, addressing both cognitive and social dimensions of language
learning, and will develop approaches for applying these ideas in authentic
classroom contexts. Through interactive learning experiences such as
micro-teaching, collaborative projects, and structured peer feedback,
students will investigate a range of teaching strategies suitable for varied
educational settings. They will also take part in reflective activities aimed
at improving instructional methods and deepening their understanding of
what constitutes effective communication. By the end of the course,
students will have the tools needed to design and deliver oral
communication lessons that actively engage learners, strengthen speaking
and listening proficiency, and nurture a supportive, student-centered
learning environment.
EDUC352
Methods of
Teaching
Reading
3
This course examines how educators can cultivate a love of reading while
addressing the diverse needs of learners. Focused on building
comprehension, critical thinking skills, and a meaningful connection to the
world through text, the course covers essential components of effective
reading instruction, including phonics, vocabulary, fluency, and
comprehension. Participants will explore the stages of reading
development, develop engaging and inclusive lesson plans, and evaluate
strategies for assessing and supporting readers from Grade 1 to Grade 9.
Special emphasis is placed on evidence-based practices, culturally
responsive teaching, and targeted interventions for struggling English
language learners. By bridging theory and practical application, this course
equips aspiring educators with the tools to foster lifelong literacy and
academic success.
EDUC353
Language
Acquisition &
Development
3
What are the mechanisms behind second language acquisition, and what
factors shape this process__ This course delves into the intricacies of
second language acquisition (SLA), analyzing core principles such as
cognitive and social influences, distinctions between first and second
language learning, and best practices for language instruction. Through
immersive activities like micro-teaching sessions, constructive peer
feedback, and reflective exercises, participants will integrate SLA theories
into practical language education scenarios. By the conclusion of the
course, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of SLA and
cultivate skills to design effective, learner-centered approaches to
language teaching.
ENGL421
Phonology &
Phonetics
3
What pedagogical approaches and knowledge are essential for guiding
English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners toward clear and confident
oral communication__ This course is designed to provide a comprehensive
foundation in English phonology while equipping participants with the
pedagogical competencies required to teach pronunciation effectively in
diverse instructional contexts. Anchored in the principles of
Communicative Language Teaching (CLT), the course offers an in-depth
exploration of key phonological featuresâincluding phonemes, stress
patterns, rhythm, and intonationâwhile emphasizing the integration of
theoretical knowledge with practical classroom strategies. Learners will
engage in the design of communicative and learner-centered pronunciation
activities, learn to incorporate pronunciation into broader language
instruction, and cultivate learners' intelligibility and speaking confidence.
Upon successful completion of the course, participants will demonstrate a
thorough understanding of English phonological systems, apply effective
pronunciation teaching methodologies, and showcase their instructional
skills through the development and delivery of a comprehensive
pronunciation lesson plan in a microteaching session.
EDUC425
Assessment &
Evaluation in
Language
Learning
3
This course offers a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and
principles of language assessment and evaluation, covering both qualitative
and quantitative strategies for measuring language proficiency. Students
will engage with current practices and emerging technologiesâincluding
the integration of generative AIâto gain practical insights into designing
and interpreting language assessment tools. Using real-life scenarios,
practical tasks, and interactive discussions, the course fosters the
development of a strong theoretical and practical foundation in essential
assessment standards, such as validity, reliability, and fairness. Students
will refine their ability to critically examine language assessment practices
and tools while designing context-appropriate evaluation strategies. By the
end of the course, students will be equipped to assess language learning
outcomes with greater precision, create effective evaluation instruments,
and apply their learning across varied learning contexts, ultimately
enhancing their professional competence in language teaching and
assessment.

and actions shape how students learn and grow__ This course dives into the
core ideas of educational psychology, helping students understand how
learners develop. By grasping these key areas, students will learn to create
lively lessons and implement effective classroom management strategies.
Throughout this course, students will explore the basic ideas and important
theories about how people develop, including their thinking, social lives,
moral understanding, and behaviors. The approach emphasizes seeing the
whole picture, encouraging students to use what they learn in real
classrooms. Through interesting talks, discussions, and hands-on activities,
students will gain the tools and knowledge needed to support students'
growth at every stage. By looking at both the theories and how they work in
practice, students will see how different teaching methods affect learning
outcomes. This course aims to equip future educators with the skills to
enhance learning across diverse educational settings, fostering both student
growth and their own professional journey.

course takes students on a fascinating journey through the crucial stages of
child development, exploring the major theories and cutting-edge research
from the very beginning of life all the way to the start of formal schooling. It
will delve into the powerful forces that shape young lives, including the
dynamics within families, the impact of school settings, and the influence of
socioeconomic factors. Ultimately, this course aims to give students a solid
grasp of the key ideas and areas in childhood and adolescent development,
along with effective teaching approaches that truly support the well-being of
young learners.

How do we gain insight into the psychological mechanisms that drive
learning, and how can we leverage this understanding to improve
educational practices__ This course delves into foundational theories of
learning and cognitive processes, with particular emphasis on key concepts
such as memory, motivation, metacognition, and self-regulation. Through a
range of interactive and applied learning experiencesâincluding lesson
planning, case analyses, and collaborative dialogueâstudents will translate
theoretical knowledge into practical strategies for addressing real-world
educational challenges. By the end of the course, students will be equipped
to design effective learning environments, selec_t and implement
appropriate instructional techniques, and correct common misconceptions,
all while nurturing both critical and creative thinking. Ultimately, the course
prepares students to cultivate learner-centered classrooms that support deep
and lasting knowledge acquisition.

practice. Designed to cultivate reflective, adaptable, and student-centered
teaching approaches, the practicum emphasizes experiential learning
through 60 hours of structured classroom observation, tailored to the
specific focus of each education major. Throughout the course, students
will explore a variety of instructional methods, classroom management
strategies, and assessment tools, while engaging with constructivist, brain-
based, and metacognitive learning theories. Grounded in a philosophy of
inclusivity and lifelong learning, the course integrates reflective dialogue,
observation tools, evaluation rubrics, and the development of a
professional portfolio to track student growth. By the end of the practicum,
students will be able to critically evaluate teaching practices, contribute to
inclusive and effective learning environments, and clearly express their
evolving instructional philosophyâpreparing them to meet the diverse
and ever-changing demands of todayâs educational landscape.
EDUC452
Teaching
Practicum II
3
This course serves as a crucial follow-up to Teaching Practicum I,
advancing students' instructional competence and deepening their
practical teaching experience within authentic classroom environments.
Building on the foundational insights gained in the first practicum, this
course transitions students from primarily observational roles to active
teaching responsibilities. Emphasizing the integration of theory and
practice, the course enhances students' abilities in lesson planning,
differentiated instruction, classroom management, and learner
engagement, preparing them to address the varied needs of todayâs
diverse classrooms. Through immersive teaching placements, students will
observe, reflect, and take on teaching duties while applying pedagogical
theories to real-world contexts. Core topics include advanced instructional
strategies such as constructivist methods, active learning, and problem-
based learning. Students will also explore classroom differentiation,
assessment techniques, and inclusive teaching practices to meet the needs
of all learners. Throughout the course, students will refine their capacity to
design and deliver comprehensive, student-centered lesson plans that
promote critical thinking, creativity, and participation. Assignments
include microteaching, full-class teaching demonstrations, and the
development of a professional teaching portfolio. Continuous feedback
from mentor teachers and peers supports reflective practice and ongoing
improvement. By the end of the course, students will have confidently
applied effective teaching strategies in classroom settings, built a
reflective portfolio featuring lesson plans and teaching artifacts, and
developed key professional tools such as CVs and cover letters. This
practicum equips aspiring educators with the skills, confidence, and
professional readiness required for successful entry into the teaching
profession.
BIOL200
General Biology
I
3
This course aims to familiarize the student with the organization and
classification of living systems. The covered topics include mainly the cell
structure and function, cell division, cell biochemistry, cellular respiration,
DNA structure and protein function, as well as animal development and
classification. This course has a separate one credit-laboratory component.
 
CHEM200
General
Chemistry
3
This course is a first semester course, intended for students who desire to
acquire the basic principles in chemistry. The emphasis of the course will
be on the fundamental principles of general chemistry, which include
terminology, qualitative concepts and quantitative skills. The general
topics included in this course are: Quantum Theory of the Atom; Electrons
and Periodicity; Bonding; Molecular Geometry; Hybridization; Acid/base
Chemistry; Kinetics and reactions mechanism and Solubility and Complex
ion equilibria.
EDUC332
Elementary
Level Science
Concepts
3
Elementary Level Science Concepts offers an in-depth exploration of core
scientific concepts and instructional strategies essential for teaching
science at the elementary level. It emphasizes inquiry-based and
constructivist approaches, aligning with the 6E instructional model to
foster scientific literacy and critical thinking. Students will investigate key
ideas from physical, life, and earth/space sciences while developing lesson
plans that reflect current best practices in science education.
EDUC363
Teaching
Sciences in
Basic Education
3
This course prepares aspiring educators to inspire and empower learners
in the primary and middle grades through effective science teaching. By
cultivating essential knowledge, skills, and innovative strategies,
participants will learn to nurture curiosity and a profound appreciation for
scientific exploration. The course emphasizes active learning through
hands-on experiments, collaborative projects, and thoughtful reflection,
equipping future educators to excel as science instructors. Through a focus
on inquiry-driven teaching methods and the integration of cutting-edge
technology, participants will be trained to foster inclusive, engaging, and
dynamic learning environments that encourage scientific literacy and
critical thinking.
EDUC364
Fundamentals of
Physical
Sciences
3
This introductory course explores the foundational principles of the
physical sciences, guiding students through an exciting journey across key
topics such as measurement, force and motion, work and energy, waves
and sound, optics and wave phenomena, electricity and magnetism,
chemical elements, chemical reactions, and organic chemistry. Through
dynamic, hands-on activities and thought-provoking experiments, students
will develop a robust understanding of scientific principles. The course
emphasizes inquiry-based learning and fosters critical thinking, creativity,
and problem-solving skills. By connecting theory to real-world applications,
this course inspires curiosity and demonstrates the impact of physical
science in everyday life.
EDUC365
Teaching
Sciences with
Technology
3
How can future educators effectively leverage technology to enhance
science instruction and student understanding__ This course explores the
dynamic intersection between science education and technology, equipping
pre-service teachers with both theoretical knowledge and practical
strategies for tech-infused instruction. Through an inquiry-driven, hands-on
approach, students will examine how tools like simulations, virtual labs,
and interactive digital platforms can transform learning in early years,
primary, and intermediate science classrooms. Emphasis is placed on
designing learner-centered, standards-aligned science experiences that
promote exploration, engagement, and critical thinking. By the end of the
course, learners will be able to assess, apply, and reflect on technology
integration practices, preparing them to become innovative science
educators.
EDUC432
Basics of Earth
Sciences
3
This course offers an immersive introduction to the core concepts of earth
sciences, encompassing geology, meteorology, oceanography, and
astronomy. By emphasizing inquiry-based learning and integrating cutting-
edge technology, the course equips aspiring educators with the skills to
design stimulating and inclusive earth science learning environments.
Through exploration of fundamental principles, hands-on activities, and the
creation of innovative lesson plans, students will cultivate the expertise
and confidence needed to inspire young learners and deepen their
appreciation for the dynamic processes shaping our planet and beyond.
EDUC433
Inquiry-Based
Science
Education
3
This course delves into the principles and practices of inquiry-based
science education, highlighting the importance of inquiry in fostering
scientific literacy. It aims to equip future educators with the essential
knowledge and skills to implement inquiry-based teaching strategies
effectively in the classroom. Students will participate in hands-on activities,
create lesson plans, and explore various inquiry-based approaches to
science education. Key topics include enhancing scientific literacy,
encouraging scientific discourse, organizing cooperative learning, and
evaluating students' reasoning and problem-solving abilities using the
SOLO Taxonomy.

Bachelor of Translation and Interpretation
Major Requirements
Code
Title
Credits
Description
TRNS402
Literary
Translation
3
Literary translation is one of the pillars of the field. In this course, students
will acquire techniques for translating literary texts in two linguistic
combinations: B-A/A-B. They will work on excerpts from novels, poetry and
prose works. Alongside the practical aspect of this course, a theoretical
research and approaches will be implemented. Students will be able to
grasp the essence of literary work and better understand the role of the
translator and the author.
TRNS411
Translation of
Legal & Official
Documents
3
Preparing students for the marketplace goes together with learning the
techniques of legal translation. Advanced techniques for translating
specialized legal texts from Arabic into English and vice versa will allow
students to understand the basic concepts of legal work. They will build a
database of terms allowing them to be ready for the market. This course
focuses on the kind of documents translated by sworn legal translators and
on the importance of preserving the source text form in the target text. This
course covers a variety of texts including contracts, decrees, lawsuits,
conventions, agreements and various types of certificates.
TRNS302
Media
Translation
3
Media translation is one of the main fields in which the translator role is
very significant. Students will acquire techniques for translating
journalistic texts in two linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B. In this course,
students not only translate press releases, briefs, reports, articles and
analyses, but also do copywriting. Students will become familiar with the
different styles, formats, and features of media language. This is in addition
to enriching the studentsÃ¢â¬â¢ general knowledge.
TRNS312
On-Sight
Interpretation
3
Interpretation is the oral translation of texts in real time. On-sight
interpretation transforms a written message into a spoken message.
Students will acquire the basic techniques of on-sight interpretation in two
linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B: This course seeks to give students an
insight into the world of oral translation or interpretation, more specifically
on-Sight Interpretation. It doesn’t aim to prepare market-ready
interpreters, but rather to help students acquire fluency and quick-
wittedness and train them to translate without dictionaries. Students will
also be exposed to different interpretation scenarios and develop relevant
terminology lists.
TRNS400
Economic
Translation
3
Each translation field has its own challenges and techniques. As part of the
scientific and technical world, Economic translation has its own
specifications. Students will acquire techniques for translating economic
texts in two linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B. During this course, students
will learn basic economic principles and terminology. It covers a variety of
topics including understanding world economy, stock markets, banking and
modern economy-related matters.
TRNS410
Medical
Translation
3
Looking back at the history of translation, it has always been related to the
medical field thanks to its importance in spreading knowledge. Students
will work on understanding medical concepts prior to translating medical
texts in two linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B. Students are trained in the
protocols of translating medical texts of the type that is usually
communicated to the general reader through mass media (new inventions,
modern research, diseases, etc) or those addressed to the medical field
experts. This course acquaints students with basic medical terminology and
various kinds of texts that they might deal with on the translation market
(prescriptions, pharmaceutical reports, awareness-raising brochures,
hospitalization reports, etc).
TRNS412
Translation
Senior Project
3
The senior project is a combination of theories and practice, in which
students will apply everything they gathered throughout their academic
years. This course is based on a theoretical research and analytical
description of various problems and challenges that students faced during
the translation of one chapter of a book. This theory-based research paper
submitted to a supervisor/first reader and an in-house second reader is an
academic milestone.
TRNS404
Introduction to
Translation
Studies
3
Translation studies is the translator’s way to discover all the mechanisms
related to this profession. This course will cover major theories and
approaches in translation and will introduce students to the theoretical
aspect of their major, giving them a taste of some groundbreaking
theoretical research in the domains of Translation Studies and Applied
Linguistics. This course is an opportunity for students to dive deeper in
their major, recognizing its various challenges.
TRNS310
Scientific and
Technical
Translation
3
Each translation field has its own challenges and techniques. Students will
be introduced to different techniques for translating scientific and technical
texts in two linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B. They will be trained in the
protocols of translating scientific and technical texts of the type that is
usually communicated to the general reader through mass media,
especially current discoveries and interesting topics that have gone viral.
This course acquaints students with basic technical terminology and
various kinds of texts in preparation for the job market.
ENGL415
Editing &
Proofreading:
English
3
As this course is considered a sequence to ENGL305, students will
implement all the grammar and writing skills they previously acquired. As
for the purpose of this course, it is to familiarize students with proofreading
and editing skills in order to improve their overall writing ability.
Throughout the semester, they will learn the difference between
proofreading and editing while getting hands-on experience in all stages of
the writing process including techniques of academic reporting. The course
will focus on specialized writing, proofreading and revision techniques.
FREN400
Upper French:
B1-3 __ DELF B1
3
Ce 
cours favorise l’implication des apprenants dans leur apprentissage de
la langue française. Il leur permet de développer leurs aptitudes
d’observation et de réflexion, ils deviennent de plus en plus autonomes. En
passant ce cours les apprenants deviennent prêts pour passer les épreuves
du DELF B1, ils seront sujets à l’examen DELF B1, dont la note sera
retenue pour le prochain cours du FREN485.
FREN410
Upper French:
B2- FLE
3
Ce cours s’adresse aux apprenants ayant acquis le niveau B1 permet
l’acquisition des compétences orales et écrites en plaçant les apprenants en
situation et en leur fournissant les instruments nécessaires pour échanger
d’une manière autonome tant dans la classe ou dans un milieu francophone,
et également en leur enseignant la langue et la culture dans tous ses
aspects, afin de se préparer ultérieurement aux épreuves de D.E.LF.B2.
TRNS403
Translation of
Various Domains
FR-AR/ AR-FR
3
As students acquire more advanced levels of the French language, they will
be exposed to more specialized texts. In this course, students will work on
the translation of texts in two linguistic combinations: Fr-Ar/Ar-Fr. The
course targets most domains of translation with a focus on the different
approaches used for understanding and formulating the target text into a
translator’s C language. Students will also learn how to be flexible when
translating into a language pair they are less fluent at and will acquire the
necessary skills to overcome translation challenges that arise in this
regard.
TRNS311
Translation of
UN Documents
3
Translators work in different settings and organizations. They must be
capable of translating documents relevant to international organizations
such as the UN. In this course, students learn techniques for translating
UN- related texts in two linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B: This course aims
to prepare students for competitive translation exams, namely the
competitive examination administered by the United Nations for Arabic
translators every year. It covers a variety of domains (technical, legal,
medical, economic, etc) and trains students on understanding texts by
means of rhetorical analysis not with the help of dictionaries whose use is
usually forbidden in all competitive exams. Students will also learn the
terminology usually used at the UN.
TRNS401
Consecutive
Interpretation
3
After acquiring the basic skills of on-sight interpretation, students will learn
the basic techniques of consecutive interpretation in two linguistic
combinations: B-A/A-B. This course seeks to give students an insight into
the world of oral translation or interpretation, more specifically
Consecutive Interpretation. It does not aim to prepare market-ready
interpreters, but rather to help students acquire fluency and quick-
wittedness and train them to translate without dictionaries. Students will
learn the basics of terminology research and form their own term base.
TRNS413
Simultaneous
Interpretation
3
After acquiring the basic skills of on-sight and consecutive interpretation,
students will learn the basic techniques of simultaneous interpretation in
two linguistic combinations: B-A/A-B. This course seeks to give students an
insight into the world of oral translation or interpretation, more specifically
Simultaneous Interpretation, which is the most popular kind of
interpretation. This course is introductory and so it does not aim to prepare
market-ready interpreters, but rather to help students acquire fluency and
quick-wittedness and train them to translate without dictionaries. Students
will work on in-depth terminology research and form their own term base
related to the topics covered.

This course emphasizes on the language skills in listening, reading,
speaking, and writing by focusing on the application of simple grammatical
concepts. The student will learn to use Spanish vocabulary for practical and
everyday use; speak with sufficient correct pronunciation to be understood;
read and write a simple paragraph in Spanish and become informed about
relevant aspects of Hispanic culture.

3
In the field of translation, the translator is exposed to a variety of fields from
general to specific. The skills a translator acquires when translating general
texts are necessary to move on to more specialized domains. In this course,
students learn the basic techniques for translating non-specialized texts from
Arabic into English: This course focuses on the different approaches used for
understanding the source text and formulating the target text. It also pays
special attention to mistakes commonly made by translators.
SPAN300
Spanish level 3
3
As a direct continuation of the Span210 course, this course builds upon the
previously acquired knowledge of the Spanish language. With a specific
focus on reading, speaking, listening, and writing skills within everyday
contexts, students will continue to explore and expand their linguistic
abilities. The primary aim of this course is to solidify and consolidate the
skills students have developed in their initial encounters with the Spanish
language in previous levels. By doing so, it equips them with the necessary
tools to successfully achieve the objectives outlined in the previous course.
Through engaging lessons and activities, students will further develop their
language proficiency and enhance their ability to navigate real-life situations
in Spanish.
SPAN210
Spanish level 2
3
Building upon the foundation laid in the SPAN200 course, this course serves
as a continuation with a primary focus on addressing the most common
grammatical challenges at this level. Students will delve into the core
elements of Spanish grammar to solidify their understanding, while applying
these grammatical concepts to discuss the present and past. Additionally,
the course places a strong emphasis on enhancing written expression skills.
The overarching goal of this course is to develop students' communicative
and intercultural competences. This includes expanding their vocabulary and
honing their language usage in various activities such as listening, reading
comprehension, speaking, and writing, all at the elementary level. By
engaging with this course, students will not only gain access to the Spanish-
speaking world but also enhance their academic training and boost their
confidence to progress to higher levels of proficiency.

English into Arabic. The course focuses on the different approaches used for
understanding the source text and formulating the target text. It also pays
special attention to mistakes commonly made by translators.

Technical

3

Description
EDUC505
Assessment
and Evaluation
3
Assessment and evaluation are essential components of any educational
program. This course is designed to provide students with an understanding
of the principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education.
The course will cover various topics related to assessment and evaluation,
including: Theoretical foundations of assessment and evaluation, Types of
assessment and evaluation Assessment and evaluation methods, The role of
assessment and evaluation in curriculum development, The role of
assessment and evaluation in instructional design, The use of technology in
assessment and evaluation, Ethical issues in assessment and evaluation,
Validity and reliability in assessment and evaluation, Data analysis and
interpretation in assessment and evaluation, Reporting and communicating
assessment and evaluation results. Throughout the course, students will
engage in class activities and projects that will allow them to apply their
knowledge and skills in assessment and evaluation. They will also have the
opportunity to analyze and evaluate current assessment and evaluation
practices in education and propose improvements based on their learning. By
the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of the
principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education, and they
will be able to design, implement, and evaluate effective assessment and
evaluation strategies.
EDUC530
Educational
Media and
Technology
3
Educational Media and Technology is a course that focuses on the role of
various forms of media and technology in education. The course is designed
to help students develop a critical understanding of the impact of technology
on teaching and learning. The course covers a range of topics, including the
history and evolution of educational technology, theories of learning and
technology, the design and development of instructional materials, and the
use of various media and technologies in educational contexts. Through a
combination of lectures, readings, discussions, and hands-on projects,
students will develop practical skills in the use of various media and
technologies for teaching and learning. They will also learn how to evaluate
and select appropriate media and technologies based on the needs of
learners and the goals of instruction. At the end of the course, students will
be able to apply their knowledge and skills in the development and
implementation of effective educational media and technology programs.
They will also be able to critically analyze the impact of media and technology
on teaching and learning and make informed decisions about the use of these
tools in educational contexts.
EDUC513
Research
Methodology
& Dissertation
Preparation
3
This course creates a framework for research projects by introducing
relevant approaches and strategies related to educational research. This
course provides students with theoretical concepts and practical skills. It
equips them with skills required for evaluating, planning, conducting and
reporting research studies. The structure of this course follows a cumulative
approach of practicing the content introduced step-by-step. To culminate the
final step, students will learn to a write comprehensive research proposal and
will be ready to conduct their own research study. This course is a
prerequisite for EDUC580 and EDUC695.
EDUC504
Classroom
Dynamics
3
This course is designed to equip teachers with the necessary knowledge and
skills to effectively manage a classroom environment that fosters learning,
respect, and positive student behavior. Throughout the course, students will
explore various theories, techniques, and strategies that are proven to
promote student engagement and academic success while maintaining a safe
and orderly classroom environment. The course begins with an introduction
to the principles of classroom management, including the importance of
establishing clear expectations and rules, creating a positive classroom
culture, and building relationships with students. Students will also learn
how to use positive reinforcement and motivation to encourage desired
behaviors and academic progress. In subsequent modules, the course will
cover a range of topics related to classroom management, including
classroom organization, instructional strategies, student assessment, and
intervention techniques. Students will learn how to manage various types of
behavior, including disruptive behavior, off-task behavior, and challenging
behavior. They will also learn how to communicate effectively with students,
parents, and colleagues, and how to work collaboratively to create a positive
and productive learning environment. By the end of the course, students will
have gained a deep understanding of the principles and practices of effective
classroom management. They will be able to apply these skills in a variety of
educational settings, from early childhood to secondary education, and will
be well-prepared to create and maintain a safe, engaging, and productive
classroom environment. The concepts in this course are reinforced by in-class
discussions, group work, and authentic activities.
EDUC512
Curriculum
Design &
Evaluation
3
The course promotes the identification of curriculum issues in the field of education
and encourages students to develop effective curriculum models to meet the
challenge of implementing an instructional program in today's multicultural and
diverse educational system. A comprehensive analysis of the process of curriculum
development is presented through an examination of its theoretical dimensions. The
relationship between curriculum, assessment and instruction is then explored
enabling students to research various curriculum models and pedagogies and
demonstrate methods of evaluating instructions and curricula. 
EDUC519
Content Area
Education for
TESL Students
3
This is one of the core masters courses in the Education Department. It is
designed for all students pursuing their MA in TESL. The course is intended
to prepare students to work collaboratively with teachers who are teaching
different subjects in English. First, students will focus on certain theoretical
principles related to the teaching of English through content and their
practical implications. Later in the course, students will be introduced to the
Sheltered Instruction Observation Protocol (SIOP) model which is one of the
models mostly followed in the domain of Content-Based Language Teaching
(CBLT). This course has no specific prerequisites. Also, it is not a prerequisite
for any other course.
EDUC503
Philosophy of
Education
3
This comprehensive course invites students to dive into the fascinating world
of educational philosophy and learning psychology. The "Philosophy of
Education and Psychology of Learning" course aims to provide learners with
a deep understanding of the theories and principles that underlie educational
practices and human learning. The course is grounded in the belief that a
strong foundation in both philosophy and psychology is essential for
educators to make informed decisions about teaching practices and create
effective learning environments. Learners will explore topics such as the
epistemic aims of education, moral and political aims of education,
behaviorism, and constructivism. Through a combination of lectures,
readings, discussions, and assessments, including a midterm exam, a project,
and a final exam, learners will engage with the material and demonstrate
their understanding. Upon successful completion of the course, learners will
be able to critically evaluate various philosophical and psychological theories
of education, apply these theories to real-world educational settings, and
develop a more comprehensive understanding of the complexities of human
learning.

EDUC671
Graduate
Research
Project
3
EDUC694 is a mini research project course designed to teach students research
skills through a combination of readings, lectures and research activities or
projects. The purpose of such research projects is for the student to apply what is
being taught (i.e. use skills outside of the classroom) rather than to contribute to
existing research literature in a field. Students planning to use a class-based
project as part of senior masters, independent study project, or for submitting it
for off campus publication or presentation must follow the IRB review procedures
before commencing the project.
EDUC507
Advanced
Methods of
Teaching
Humanities and
Language
3
This course is designed to assist Teaching Diploma (TD) students in their
study of a range of approaches, issues and practices in the teaching of
Humanities and Language. It introduces the necessary pedagogical
knowledge and practical understanding necessary that help in creating
effective teaching and productive learning environment. It also provides
graduate students with a wide source of classroom theories and strategies to
change how teachers think about teaching and to change how they actually
teach. Besides, this course includes practical issues such as how to involve
diverse learners in the teaching-learning process; how to develop
Humanities and Language skills through different instructions; and how to
teach different cognitive, affective and psychomotor skills through effective
techniques. Through this course, graduate students will broaden their
repertoire of teaching skills that they can refer to develop their own
profession. The different objectives of this course will be reinforced through
classroom discussions, subjective assignments, case studies and authentic
context. 
EDUC602
Literacy and
Language
Development
3
This course discusses the research on emergent literacy and language
development in early childhood. It aims at equipping teacher candidates with
the necessary knowledge and skills to design appropriate literacy learning
environments and experiences for young learners (zero to 8 years old). The
concepts in this course are reinforced by in-class discussions, group work,
and authentic activities. This is an advanced course; therefore,  students will
be expected to have a reading background in early literacy. This course is
required for the Reading Specialist Endorsement.
EDUC604
Applied
Linguistics
3
EDUC610 is an introduction to applied linguistics. It focuses on the description of
language and language use through addressing subtopics of particular relevance
to language teaching
: grammar and syntax, vocabulary, discourse analysis of
formal and informal spoken/written texts, pragmatics, semantics and corpus
linguistics. It also highlights essential areas of enquiry in applied linguistics,
mainly sociolinguistics and psycholinguistics. The course highlights the most
common language assessments. This course has no specific prerequisites. Also, it
is not a prerequisite for any other course.
EDUC605
Teaching
Practices
3
This course equips students with theoretical and practical teaching
principles and provides a foundation for understanding the relationship
between planning, implementing, and assessing student learning. The

EDUC530
Educational
Media and
Technology
3
Educational Media and Technology is a course that focuses on the role of
various forms of media and technology in education. The course is designed
to help students develop a critical understanding of the impact of technology
on teaching and learning. The course covers a range of topics, including the
history and evolution of educational technology, theories of learning and
technology, the design and development of instructional materials, and the
use of various media and technologies in educational contexts. Through a
combination of lectures, readings, discussions, and hands-on projects,
students will develop practical skills in the use of various media and
technologies for teaching and learning. They will also learn how to evaluate
and select appropriate media and technologies based on the needs of
learners and the goals of instruction. At the end of the course, students will
be able to apply their knowledge and skills in the development and
implementation of effective educational media and technology programs.
They will also be able to critically analyze the impact of media and technology
on teaching and learning and make informed decisions about the use of these
tools in educational contexts.
EDUC513
Research
Methodology
& Dissertation
Preparation
3
This course creates a framework for research projects by introducing
relevant approaches and strategies related to educational research. This
course provides students with theoretical concepts and practical skills. It
equips them with skills required for evaluating, planning, conducting and
reporting research studies. The structure of this course follows a cumulative
approach of practicing the content introduced step-by-step. To culminate the
final step, students will learn to a write comprehensive research proposal and
will be ready to conduct their own research study. This course is a
prerequisite for EDUC580 and EDUC695.
EDUC504
Classroom
Dynamics
3
This course is designed to equip teachers with the necessary knowledge and
skills to effectively manage a classroom environment that fosters learning,
respect, and positive student behavior. Throughout the course, students will
explore various theories, techniques, and strategies that are proven to
promote student engagement and academic success while maintaining a safe
and orderly classroom environment. The course begins with an introduction
to the principles of classroom management, including the importance of
establishing clear expectations and rules, creating a positive classroom
culture, and building relationships with students. Students will also learn how
to use positive reinforcement and motivation to encourage desired behaviors
and academic progress. In subsequent modules, the course will cover a range
of topics related to classroom management, including classroom
organization, instructional strategies, student assessment, and intervention
techniques. Students will learn how to manage various types of behavior,
including disruptive behavior, off-task behavior, and challenging behavior.
They will also learn how to communicate effectively with students, parents,
and colleagues, and how to work collaboratively to create a positive and
productive learning environment. By the end of the course, students will have
gained a deep understanding of the principles and practices of effective
classroom management. They will be able to apply these skills in a variety of
educational settings, from early childhood to secondary education, and will
be well-prepared to create and maintain a safe, engaging, and productive
classroom environment. The concepts in this course are reinforced by in-class
discussions, group work, and authentic activities.
EDUC505
Assessment
and Evaluation
3
Assessment and evaluation are essential components of any educational
program. This course is designed to provide students with an understanding
of the principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education.
The course will cover various topics related to assessment and evaluation,
including: Theoretical foundations of assessment and evaluation, Types of
assessment and evaluation Assessment and evaluation methods, The role of
assessment and evaluation in curriculum development, The role of
assessment and evaluation in instructional design, The use of technology in
assessment and evaluation, Ethical issues in assessment and evaluation,
Validity and reliability in assessment and evaluation, Data analysis and
interpretation in assessment and evaluation, Reporting and communicating
assessment and evaluation results. Throughout the course, students will
engage in class activities and projects that will allow them to apply their
knowledge and skills in assessment and evaluation. They will also have the
opportunity to analyze and evaluate current assessment and evaluation
practices in education and propose improvements based on their learning. By
the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of the
principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education, and they
will be able to design, implement, and evaluate effective assessment and
evaluation strategies.
EDUC512
Curriculum
Design &
Evaluation
3
The course promotes the identification of curriculum issues in the field of education
and encourages students to develop effective curriculum models to meet the
challenge of implementing an instructional program in today's multicultural and
diverse educational system. A comprehensive analysis of the process of curriculum
development is presented through an examination of its theoretical dimensions. The
relationship between curriculum, assessment and instruction is then explored
enabling students to research various curriculum models and pedagogies and
demonstrate methods of evaluating instructions and curricula. 
EDUC516
Counseling:
Theory and
Practice
3
The aim of the course is to familiarize students with diverse approaches to
psychotherapy used in schools and clinics around the world, and to convey
the necessary practical skills required for their application. Through lectures,
and discussions, the course will provide students with relevant knowledge of
major schools of psychotherapy, their respective uses and usefulness, and
their relevance for dealing with problems faced by students, teachers, and
people in general. The focus of application and real-life examples will be on
academic settings.
EDUC503
Philosophy of
Education
3
This comprehensive course invites students to dive into the fascinating world
of educational philosophy and learning psychology. The "Philosophy of
Education and Psychology of Learning" course aims to provide learners with
a deep understanding of the theories and principles that underlie educational
practices and human learning. The course is grounded in the belief that a
strong foundation in both philosophy and psychology is essential for
educators to make informed decisions about teaching practices and create
effective learning environments. Learners will explore topics such as the
epistemic aims of education, moral and political aims of education,
behaviorism, and constructivism. Through a combination of lectures,
readings, discussions, and assessments, including a midterm exam, a project,
and a final exam, learners will engage with the material and demonstrate
their understanding. Upon successful completion of the course, learners will
be able to critically evaluate various philosophical and psychological theories
of education, apply these theories to real-world educational settings, and
develop a more comprehensive understanding of the complexities of human
learning.

EDUC671
Graduate
Research Project
3
EDUC694 is a mini research project course designed to teach students research
skills through a combination of readings, lectures and research activities or
projects. The purpose of such research projects is for the student to apply what is
being taught (i.e. use skills outside of the classroom) rather than to contribute to
existing research literature in a field. Students planning to use a class-based
project as part of senior masters, independent study project, or for submitting it
for off campus publication or presentation must follow the IRB review
procedures before commencing the project.
EDUC605
Teaching
Practices
3
This course equips students with theoretical and practical teaching
principles and provides a foundation for understanding the relationship
between planning, implementing, and assessing student learning. The
experiences embedded in this course enable students to construct their
framework for teaching and will prepare them to make sound and strong
teaching decisions. The concepts in this course are reinforced by in-class
discussions, group work, and authentic activities. This course has no
specific prerequisites. Also, it is not a prerequisite for any other course.
EDUC506
Practicum in
Educational
Management &
Leadership
3
Practicum in Educational Management & Leadership course aims at developing
capabilities and skills of students related to the design, promotion and delivery of
educational programs.  It provides both an in-depth presentation of leadership
theory and a discussion of how it applies to real-life situations.
EDUC601
Personnel and
Human Resource
Management
3
This course will provide students with an overview of different disciplines
under human resource (HR) management, how it is integrated within the
organizational context, and how it is changing in response to trends in the
workplace. The course illustrates HR concepts and techniques, HR’s role in
strategic planning and improved organizational performance, and the
competencies required of HR managers. Human resources play a key role
in helping companies meet the challenges of global competition and achieve
flexibility within the workplace.
Strategic objectives to lower costs, improve productivity, and increase
organizational effectiveness are changing the way every part of the
organization, including the HR department, does business. Managers do not
want to make personnel mistakes, such as hiring the wrong person, having
their company taken to court because of discriminatory actions, or
committing unfair labor practices. HRM can improve profits and
performance by hiring the right people and motivating them appropriately.
EDUC603
Strategic
Planning in
Education
3
A strategic plan in education is the physical product of the strategic
planning process. It embodies the guiding orientations on how to run an
education system within a larger national development perspective, which
is evolving by nature and often involves constraints. The course aims at
examining planning processes used by leaders, educational executives, and
planners to direct educational change and improvement through
approaches and models designed to address mega, macro and micro goals
of education. The course content provides students with the methods and
techniques for restructuring and revitalizing education and the operational
perspectives of planning in modern organizations.

course emphasizing workplace and technical communication and editing

preparing students for different systems of writing in their professional
lives. Examples from the writing of workplace professionals are analyzed

and critical skills in response to texts.
