SSCI205
Introduction to
Psychology
3
This course explores brain structure and functions, including
thinking/decision making, and cognition. It examines personality
development, behavior, and intelligence.Â Students will learn about stress,
health psychology, and the nature and causes of mental disorders.
EDUC220
Principles of
Education
3
Teaching is both a creative and structured endeavor that involves
motivating, guiding, and supporting learners. This course provides a
foundational introduction to the core principles and practices of effective
teaching, setting the stage for a lifelong journey in education. Through a
combination of interactive lectures, case-based discussions, and practical
activities, students will explore essential topics such as the qualities of
effective educators, student diversity, curriculum planning, classroom
management, and the integration of educational technology. Learners will
gain the skills necessary to design dynamic, inclusive, and tech-enhanced
learning environments. They will also engage with authentic teaching
scenarios, collaborate with peers on educational tasks, and reflect on their
evolving roles as educators. By the end of the course, students will have a
clear understanding of the educatorâs impact, be equipped with evidence-
based teaching strategies, and foster a commitment to ongoing professional
development. This course empowers future educators with the knowledge,
confidence, and mindset needed to positively influence learners and
educational communities.
EDUC222
Basics of
Educational
Psychology
3
Unlocking How We Learn: How do our thinking, social interactions, values,
and actions shape how students learn and grow__ This course dives into the
core ideas of educational psychology, helping students understand how
learners develop. By grasping these key areas, students will learn to create
lively lessons and implement effective classroom management strategies.
Throughout this course, students will explore the basic ideas and important
theories about how people develop, including their thinking, social lives,
moral understanding, and behaviors. The approach emphasizes seeing the
whole picture, encouraging students to use what they learn in real
classrooms. Through interesting talks, discussions, and hands-on activities,
students will gain the tools and knowledge needed to support students'
growth at every stage. By looking at both the theories and how they work in
practice, students will see how different teaching methods affect learning
outcomes. This course aims to equip future educators with the skills to
enhance learning across diverse educational settings, fostering both student
growth and their own professional journey.
EDUC251
Development of
Children and
Adolescents
3
Ever wondered how a tiny baby transforms into a complex teenager__ This
course takes students on a fascinating journey through the crucial stages of
child development, exploring the major theories and cutting-edge research
from the very beginning of life all the way to the start of formal schooling. It
will delve into the powerful forces that shape young lives, including the
dynamics within families, the impact of school settings, and the influence of
socioeconomic factors. Ultimately, this course aims to give students a solid
grasp of the key ideas and areas in childhood and adolescent development,
along with effective teaching approaches that truly support the well-being of
young learners.
EDUC252
Psychology of
Learning
3
How do we gain insight into the psychological mechanisms that drive
learning, and how can we leverage this understanding to improve
educational practices__ This course delves into foundational theories of
learning and cognitive processes, with particular emphasis on key concepts
such as memory, motivation, metacognition, and self-regulation. Through a
range of interactive and applied learning experiencesâincluding lesson
planning, case analyses, and collaborative dialogueâstudents will translate
theoretical knowledge into practical strategies for addressing real-world
educational challenges. By the end of the course, students will be equipped
to design effective learning environments, selec_t and implement
appropriate instructional techniques, and correct common misconceptions,
all while nurturing both critical and creative thinking. Ultimately, the course
prepares students to cultivate learner-centered classrooms that support deep
and lasting knowledge acquisition.
EDUC253
Technology
Integration in
Education
3
How can educators thoughtfully incorporate technology to boost student
achievement and engagement__ This course delves into the evolving role of
technology in the classroom, focusing on key themes like technology-
enhanced instruction, digital tools for differentiated learning, and the latest
innovations in educational tech. Through experiential learning, collaborative
projects, and case-based analysis, students will connect theory to practice by
integrating digital tools into authentic educational contexts. By the end of
the course, learners will be equipped to choose and implement appropriate
technologies across diverse educational settings, and design learner-
centered, tech-infused lessons that foster deep engagement and academic
success.
EDUC254
Basics of
Assessment &
Evaluation
3
Assessment of Learning offers a comprehensive exploration of both the
theoretical frameworks and research-based practices that inform effective
assessment in educational settings. Designed for future educators, the
course develops the competencies necessary to design, implement, and
evaluate a variety of assessment strategies that enhance teaching and
learning while promoting equity and inclusion. Grounded in contemporary
theories of learning and supported by empirical studies, this course
examines key principles of educational measurement, including validity,
reliability, fairness, and utility. Students will engage with a range of
assessment typesâformative, summative, diagnostic, and performance-
basedâalong with tools such as rubrics, standardized tests, and digital
assessment platforms. Emphasis is placed on aligning assessments with
instructional objectives and curriculum standards, using assessment data to
inform pedagogical decisions, and integrating culturally responsive and
inclusive practices. Through a combination of interactive lectures, case study
analysis, collaborative tasks, and practical workshops, students will gain
hands-on experience in constructing assessment tools, interpreting data, and
adapting assessment strategies to meet the needs of diverse learners. By the
end of the course, students will demonstrate not only a solid understanding
of foundational and contemporary theories of assessment but also the ability
to apply these principles to real-world classroom contexts in ways that
support student learning, foster motivation, and guide professional practice.
EDUC255
Fundamentals
of Curriculum
Design
3
This course provides an in-depth introduction to the core principles and
practices of curriculum design within a global educational context. Students
will engage with key topics including curriculum theory, educational
standards, and the evolving role of technology in shaping curriculum
development. Through a combination of interactive lectures, real-world case
studies, and practical activities, learners will explore how historical, cultural,
and societal factors influence curriculum and how it can be adapted to serve
diverse learning communities. By the end of the course, students will be able
to design inclusive, responsive curricula that address both local and
international educational needs. They will gain the tools to build curriculum
frameworks that encourage critical thinking, uphold educational equity, and
support continuous learning across varied educational settings.
EDUC320
Fundamentals
of Classroom
Management
3
Ever wonder how some classrooms just click, buzzing with focused energy
and a genuine love for learning__ The secret often lies in effective classroom
management â the very foundation upon which student potential is built
and a positive learning environment flourishes. This course delves into the
pivotal role of teachers as builders of such spaces, exploring how to cultivate
an atmosphere where students are not just present, but deeply engaged and
set up for success. It will uncover practical strategies for establishing a
proactive classroom where students naturally immerse themselves in tasks,
easily follow established rules and routines, and experience the focus that
comes from minimal distractions. Furthermore, this course equips future
educators with effective classroom management tools to help prepare them
for addressing disciplinary challenges and fostering a truly productive space
for learning. By the end of this course, participants will possess the tangible
skills to translate these strategies into real-world classroom settings,
ensuring a focused, supportive environment where every student can thrive.
EDUC322
Instructional
Methods
3
This course offers a comprehensive exploration of evidence-based
instructional methodologies designed to promote meaningful, inclusive, and
student-centered learning. Grounded in contemporary educational theories
and supported by empirical research, Methods of Teaching equips future
educators with the pedagogical knowledge and practical skills needed to
plan, implement, and assess effective instruction across diverse educational
settings. Participants will examine core components of instructional design,
including lesson planning aligned with learning outcomes, curriculum
standards, and learner diversity. Emphasis is placed on selecting and
adapting teaching strategies that foster active engagement, critical thinking,
and collaborative learning. Students will explore a range of instructional
modelsâsuch as direct instruction, inquiry-based learning, cooperative
learning, and differentiated instructionâand will develop competencies in
applying these models based on contextual and student-specific needs. The
course also investigates principles of classroom management, highlighting
strategies for creating safe, equitable, and productive learning
environments. Topics include managing classroom dynamics, responding to
student behavior, and cultivating positive teacher-student relationships
through proactive and restorative practices. Through lectures, case-based
learning, lesson simulations, and reflective practice, students will bridge
theory and practice, gaining the ability to make informed instructional
decisions grounded in research and real-world application. By the end of the
course, participants will be able to demonstrate a holistic understanding of
effective teaching practices and will possess a versatile instructional toolkit
to support student success in todayâs dynamic classrooms.
EDUC350
Basics of
Special
Education
3
Imagine a classroom where every student, regardless of their unique
learning needs, feels supported and empowered to thrive. This course dives
into the essential world of special education, exploring the core concepts,
legal frameworks, and practical strategies for effectively supporting diverse
learners within general education settings. Students will investigate the
wide spectrum of exceptionalities and their characteristics, from learning
disabilities to emotional and behavioral disorders, gaining critical insight
into their impact on learning and behavior. Through engaging discussions
and hands-on activities, the course will equip students with the knowledge to
implement inclusive practices and differentiate instruction effectively.
Students will learn to develop accessible lesson plans and utilize innovative
tools to cater to all students' needs. Furthermore, the course will provide a
thorough understanding of how to implement Individualized Education
Programs (IEPs) for students with special needs. By the end of the course,
students will possess a foundational understanding of special education,
enabling them to cultivate inclusive and supportive classroom environments.

art forms, effective teaching methods, and strategies for incorporating the
arts into early childhood curricula. The course highlights how arts and
crafts support holistic development by embedding social and ethical values
into creative practices that encourage self-expression and meaningful
communication.

knowledge and practical skills necessary to implement these approaches

development, creativity, and lifelong learning in young children, preparing

learning, and well-being of children from infancy through age eight. With a

covers various assessment techniques, including observational strategies,
standardized evaluations, and both formative and summative assessments.

listening abilities. It introduces key theories and pedagogical frameworks
related to oral communication, emphasizing practical techniques that
support pronunciation, listening comprehension, and spoken fluency.

instruction, addressing both cognitive and social dimensions of language
learning, and will develop approaches for applying these ideas in authentic
classroom contexts. Through interactive learning experiences such as
micro-teaching, collaborative projects, and structured peer feedback,
students will investigate a range of teaching strategies suitable for varied
educational settings. They will also take part in reflective activities aimed
at improving instructional methods and deepening their understanding of

reading instruction, including phonics, vocabulary, fluency, and

course equips aspiring educators with the tools to foster lifelong literacy

immersive activities like micro-teaching sessions, constructive peer
feedback, and reflective exercises, participants will integrate SLA theories
into practical language education scenarios. By the conclusion of the
course, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of SLA and
cultivate skills to design effective, learner-centered approaches to
language teaching.

collecting data, analyzing and interpreting results, and presenting findings.

pronunciation teaching methodologies, and showcase their instructional

as a critical bridge between educational theory and real-world classroom

through 60 hours of structured classroom observation, tailored to the

observation tools, evaluation rubrics, and the development of a

teach these concepts to elementary and middle school students using
appropriate materials and methods. The course emphasizes developing a
strong conceptual understanding and effective teaching methodologies in
geometry and measurement. Students will explore fundamental geometric
concepts, including points, lines, planes, angles, and various shapes,
alongside core measurement principles such as length, area, volume, and
angular measurement.

of diverse student populations.

proven to promote student engagement and academic success while

understanding of the principles and practices of effective classroom

educational settings, from early childhood to secondary education, and will
be well-prepared to create and maintain a safe, engaging, and productive
classroom environment. The concepts in this course are reinforced by in-
class discussions, group work, and authentic activities.

3

students in a technology-driven world__ Building on foundational knowledge
from Teaching of ICT I, this course challenges students to advance their
understanding and application of cutting-edge instructional strategies for ICT
education. Students will explore computational thinking, active-learning
models, and problem-solving strategies while engaging in lab-based teaching
and interdisciplinary lesson planning. The course emphasizes innovative
assessment techniques, collaborative learning, and the integration of emerging
technologies. Through interactive projects and reflective practices,
participants will refine their teaching methods and design impactful, inclusive
educational experiences. By the end of this course, educators will be prepared
to lead with confidence, equipping their students with the digital literacy and
critical thinking skills necessary to thrive in the 21st-century classroom.

Computer

3

practices__ This practicum provides future educators with hands-on
experience in teaching ICT, equipping them with the practical tools and
strategies needed to succeed in real-world classroom settings. Throughout this
course, students will explore methods for organizing and delivering ICT
curricula, assessing student progress, and integrating advanced technologies
to support diverse learning needs. Participants will engage in activities such as
creating lesson plans, implementing active learning strategies, and conducting

Core Requirements

Title
Credits
Description
EDUC5000
Fundamentals
of Education
2
Fundamentals of Education is a foundational course for graduate students
in a teaching diploma program, designed to deepen understanding of
educational theories, teaching methodologies, and curriculum
development. This course encourages critical analysis of educational
philosophies and explores evidence-based practices for creating effective
learning environments. Through a blend of theoretical exploration and
hands-on applications, students will prepare to engage in meaningful,
student-centered teaching practices.
EDUC5001
Classroom
Dynamics
3
This course is designed to equip teachers with the necessary knowledge
and skills to effectively manage a classroom environment that fosters
learning, respect, and positive student behavior. Throughout the course,
students will explore various theories, techniques, and strategies that are
proven to promote student engagement and academic success while
maintaining a safe and orderly classroom environment. The course begins
with an introduction to the principles of classroom management, including
the importance of establishing clear expectations and rules, creating a
positive classroom culture, and building relationships with students.
Students will also learn how to use positive reinforcement and motivation
to encourage desired behaviors and academic progress. In subsequent
modules, the course will cover a range of topics related to classroom
management, including classroom organization, instructional strategies,
student assessment, and intervention techniques. Students will learn how
to manage various types of behavior, including disruptive behavior, off-task
behavior, and challenging behavior. They will also learn how to
communicate effectively with students, parents, and colleagues, and how to
work collaboratively to create a positive and productive learning
environment. By the end of the course, students will have gained a deep
understanding of the principles and practices of effective classroom
management. They will be able to apply these skills in a variety of
educational settings, from early childhood to secondary education, and will
be well-prepared to create and maintain a safe, engaging, and productive
classroom environment. The concepts in this course are reinforced by in-
class discussions, group work, and authentic activities.
EDUC5002
Assessment in
Education:
Principles and
Practices
3
This course is designed to provide students with an understanding of the
principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education. The
course will cover various topics related to assessment and evaluation,
including: Theoretical foundations of assessment and evaluation, Types of
assessment and evaluation Assessment and evaluation methods, The role of
assessment and evaluation in curriculum development, The role of
assessment and evaluation in instructional design, The use of technology in
assessment and evaluation, Ethical issues in assessment and evaluation,
Validity and reliability in assessment and evaluation, Data analysis and
interpretation in assessment and evaluation, Reporting and communicating
assessment and evaluation results. Throughout the course, students will
engage in class activities and projects that will allow them to apply their
knowledge and skills in assessment and evaluation. They will also have the
opportunity to analyze and evaluate current assessment and evaluation
practices in education and propose improvements based on their learning.
By the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of the
principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education, and
they will be able to design, implement, and evaluate effective assessment
and evaluation strategies.
EDUC5003
Educational
Psychology:
Learning and
Teaching
3
This course provides an in-depth exploration of educational psychology,
focusing on the cognitive, social, and emotional factors that influence
student learning and development. Students will examine key theories and
research on developmental stages, motivation, learning theories, classroom
management, and assessment strategies. The course bridges theory and
practice, enabling students to apply psychological insights to design
effective teaching strategies and create supportive, engaging learning
environments. Through a mix of lectures, case studies, group discussions,
role-playing, and reflective activities, students will develop the skills
needed to enhance learning outcomes, manage diverse learning needs, and
foster positive classroom dynamics. By the end of the course, students will
be able to apply fundamental psychological principles in their teaching
practice, utilizing motivational and classroom management techniques to
support student development and achievement. In addition, students will
be equipped with a solid foundation in educational psychology, allowing
them to design and implement teaching practices that align with the
developmental and psychological needs of their students. They will be able
to assess and address a variety of learning challenges, fostering a
supportive and dynamic classroom environment
EDUC5500
Educational
Sociology
2
This course invites students to explore the dynamic relationship between
education and society through various theoretical perspectives,
emphasizing how education can both perpetuate and challenge social
inequalities. The objectives of the course include analyzing and applying
key educational theories, exploring how schools contribute to inequality
and stratification, and developing critical thinking skills to evaluate
educational practices and policies. Rooted in the belief that education is a
powerful tool for personal growth and societal change, the course
encourages active participation and critical engagement. Students will
engage in interactive discussions, mini-lectures, video clips, experiential
activities, and group exercises to bridge the gap between theory and
practice. By the end of the course, students will be able to critically analyze
educational theories, understand the impact of education on social mobility
and inequality, and apply their knowledge to real-world educational
settings. This course is designed for graduate students in
education__related fields, offering valuable insights into the intersection of
education and society.
EDUC5501
Professional
Ethics and Law
in Lebanese
Educational
System
3
This course delves into professional ethics and educational laws within the
Lebanese educational system. It equips educators with a thorough
understanding of their legal rights, responsibilities, and ethical obligations
through the study of Lebanese educational law, teachers' codes of conduct,
and ethical dilemmas in educational settings. Students will engage in
critical thinking, ethical decision-making, and practical applications of
educational policies, fostering a commitment to equitable and responsible
practices. The course employs a reflective, analytical approach, integrating
lectures, case studies, discussions, role-playing, and scenario analyses to
prepare educators for real-world challenges.
EDUC5502
Educational
Media and
Technology
3
How can educators harness the power of technology to transform learning
and engage students in meaningful ways__ This course delves into the
foundational and advanced aspects of integrating educational media and
technology into teaching. Students will explore a variety of tools and
platforms, from Google Apps and collaborative technologies to cutting-edge
artificial intelligence, to design dynamic and interactive learning
experiences. Through hands-on practice and collaborative projects,
students will learn to critically assess and selec_t appropriate technologies,
design technology-enhanced assessments, and create effective
instructional plans. Topics include technology integration models (TPACK,
SAMR), innovative tools for teaching and assessment, and current trends in
educational technology. By the end of the course, students will have
developed a mini-synthesis of research on educational technology and
gained practical experience in leveraging technology to meet diverse
learning needs. This course prepares educators to lead in the digital age,
equipping them with the skills and strategies needed to enhance
motivation, engagement, and efficacy in modern classrooms.
Major Requirements
Code
Title
Credits
Description
EDUC5110
Teaching
Drama and
Performing
Arts I
3
In the "Drama and Performing Arts" I course, students will immerse
themselves in the world of drama and explore effective methods for teaching
it to children. The course aims to equip participants with the knowledge and
skills to effectively integrate drama into a range of educational contexts,
fostering creativity, critical thinking, and personal growth in students. The
course philosophy emphasizes the importance of drama as a means of
enhancing self-expression, communication, and emotional intelligence, as
well as its potential for enriching cross-curricular learning experiences.
Participants will engage in various activities, such as forum theatre, games
and exercises, still images, and teaching in role, to expand their
understanding of diverse teaching methods. Throughout the course, students
will be assessed on their understanding of course materials, practical
application of learned skills, and ability to create lesson plans and evaluate
their effectiveness. Upon successful completion of the course, students will
have demonstrated the ability to design and implement engaging drama
lessons, adapt their teaching to different age groups and learning
environments, and assess their students' progress in drama and
communication arts.
EDUC5610
Teaching
Drama and
Performing
Arts II
3
Teaching of Drama and Performing Arts (II) is an advanced course that
deepens students' understanding of drama education and its role in
contemporary classrooms. Building upon foundational knowledge from
Teaching of Drama and Performing Arts (II), this module emphasizes the
integration of drama with aesthetic and interdisciplinary learning. Students
will explore innovative approaches to teaching drama that respond to the
needs of diverse learners in the 21st century. Through theoretical
frameworks, practical activities, and collaborative projects, participants will
develop the skills necessary to create, implement, and assess drama-based
learning experiences. By the end of the course, students will have cultivated
the ability to inspire creativity, foster ensemble collaboration, and evaluate
drama education effectively.
EDUC5611
Practicum of
Teaching
Drama and
Performing
Arts
3
Future teachers of Performing Arts and Drama will find a unique opportunity
to hone their craft and impact students' lives through this immersive and
practical course. The objective of this course is to prepare future educators in
teaching theater effectively by providing them with the necessary theoretical
knowledge and practical experience in a real school setting. This course
believes in the importance of hands- on experience and reflective practice,
allowing trainee teachers to develop their skills in creating engaging,
meaningful, and transformative learning experiences in Communication Arts
and Drama. Throughout the course, students will explore topics such as
teaching drama, approaches to text, planning lessons and schemes of work,
teaching Shakespeare, and integrating technology in drama teaching. The
course employs a combination of lectures, discussions, group work, in-class
practice, and teaching practicum in a real school setting. Students will be
required to submit practicum reports to reflect on their experiences and
improve their teaching skills. By the end of the course, students will have
gained the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to effectively teach
Communication Arts and Drama, including lesson planning, classroom
management, and assessment techniques. They will also have practical
experience in implementing various approaches and activities in a real school
setting.

EDUC5030
Teaching
Languages I
3
Understanding the way languages are learned is essential for any teacher. In
this course, students will explore both the theory and practical aspects of first
and second language acquisition. Through an in-depth analysis of key
theoriesâsuch as behaviorist, innatist, and interactionist
perspectivesâstudents will critically examine how language is acquired. The
course will delve into the factors that influence language learning, including
age, motivation, personality, and cognitive development. Students will also
explore bilingualism, language disorders, and the implications of second
language acquisition in classroom settings. By integrating both theoretical
insights and empirical research, this course equips future educators to make
informed decisions about how to approach language teaching, fostering
effective and inclusive language learning environments.
EDUC5530
Teaching
Languages
II
3
Building on the foundations of Teaching Languages I, this course transitions
from theory to practical application, offering students deeper insights into
effective language teaching. It emphasizes integrating language acquisition
theories with practical teaching methodologies, equipping students with the
skills to design, deliver, and assess lessons in all four language domains:
listening, speaking, reading, and writing. By completing this course, students
will be prepared to teach in diverse language settings, adapt instructional
strategies for varied learner needs, and foster effective, inclusive language
classrooms.
EDUC5531
Practicum
of Teaching
Languages
3
The Practicum of Teaching Languages is a practical and immersive course
designed to provide future language educators with the necessary skills and
experiences to effectively teach languages. Through hands-on teaching
opportunities in authentic classroom settings, students will refine their
pedagogical approaches, develop effective instructional strategies, and
enhance their classroom management techniques specific to each language.
Under the guidance and mentorship of experienced language instructors,
students will design, implement, and assess language lessons that cater to the
diverse needs and proficiency levels of their students. They will create
engaging activities and authentic language tasks that focus on developing
listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, while also incorporating
cultural aspects and intercultural competence. Throughout the practicum,
students will observe experienced language teachers, reflect on their teaching
practices, and receive constructive feedback to improve their instructional
skills and techniques. They will explore various methodologies and approaches,
such as communicative language teaching, task-based learning, and content-
based instruction, to foster language acquisition and fluency. The course will
also emphasize the integration of technology and digital resources into
language instruction, enabling students to enhance their teaching methods
through the use of multimedia, online platforms, and language learning
applications. Additionally, students will explore assessment strategies that
align with language proficiency standards, including formative and summative
assessments, portfolio-based evaluations, and performance-based tasks. By the
end of the course, students will have developed practical teaching experience,
refined their instructional techniques, and gained a deeper understanding of
effective language pedagogy. They will be equipped with the skills and
knowledge necessary to create dynamic and engaging language lessons that
foster language proficiency, cultural understanding, and a lifelong love for
language learning.

Core Requirements
Code
Title
Credits
Description
EDUC5000
Fundamentals
of Education
2
Fundamentals of Education is a foundational course for graduate students
in a teaching diploma program, designed to deepen understanding of
educational theories, teaching methodologies, and curriculum
development. This course encourages critical analysis of educational
philosophies and explores evidence-based practices for creating effective
learning environments. Through a blend of theoretical exploration and
hands-on applications, students will prepare to engage in meaningful,
student-centered teaching practices.
EDUC5001
Classroom
Dynamics
3
This course is designed to equip teachers with the necessary knowledge
and skills to effectively manage a classroom environment that fosters
learning, respect, and positive student behavior. Throughout the course,
students will explore various theories, techniques, and strategies that are
proven to promote student engagement and academic success while
maintaining a safe and orderly classroom environment. The course begins
with an introduction to the principles of classroom management, including
the importance of establishing clear expectations and rules, creating a
positive classroom culture, and building relationships with students.
Students will also learn how to use positive reinforcement and motivation
to encourage desired behaviors and academic progress. In subsequent
modules, the course will cover a range of topics related to classroom
management, including classroom organization, instructional strategies,
student assessment, and intervention techniques. Students will learn how
to manage various types of behavior, including disruptive behavior, off-task
behavior, and challenging behavior. They will also learn how to
communicate effectively with students, parents, and colleagues, and how to
work collaboratively to create a positive and productive learning
environment. By the end of the course, students will have gained a deep
understanding of the principles and practices of effective classroom
management. They will be able to apply these skills in a variety of
educational settings, from early childhood to secondary education, and will
be well-prepared to create and maintain a safe, engaging, and productive
classroom environment. The concepts in this course are reinforced by in-
class discussions, group work, and authentic activities.
EDUC5002
Assessment in
Education:
Principles and
Practices
3
This course is designed to provide students with an understanding of the
principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education. The
course will cover various topics related to assessment and evaluation,
including: Theoretical foundations of assessment and evaluation, Types of
assessment and evaluation Assessment and evaluation methods, The role of
assessment and evaluation in curriculum development, The role of
assessment and evaluation in instructional design, The use of technology in
assessment and evaluation, Ethical issues in assessment and evaluation,
Validity and reliability in assessment and evaluation, Data analysis and
interpretation in assessment and evaluation, Reporting and communicating
assessment and evaluation results. Throughout the course, students will
engage in class activities and projects that will allow them to apply their
knowledge and skills in assessment and evaluation. They will also have the
opportunity to analyze and evaluate current assessment and evaluation
practices in education and propose improvements based on their learning.
By the end of the course, students will have a solid understanding of the
principles and practices of assessment and evaluation in education, and
they will be able to design, implement, and evaluate effective assessment
and evaluation strategies.
EDUC5003
Educational
Psychology:
Learning and
Teaching
3
This course provides an in-depth exploration of educational psychology,
focusing on the cognitive, social, and emotional factors that influence
student learning and development. Students will examine key theories and
research on developmental stages, motivation, learning theories, classroom
management, and assessment strategies. The course bridges theory and
practice, enabling students to apply psychological insights to design
effective teaching strategies and create supportive, engaging learning
environments. Through a mix of lectures, case studies, group discussions,
role-playing, and reflective activities, students will develop the skills
needed to enhance learning outcomes, manage diverse learning needs, and
foster positive classroom dynamics. By the end of the course, students will
be able to apply fundamental psychological principles in their teaching
practice, utilizing motivational and classroom management techniques to
support student development and achievement. In addition, students will
be equipped with a solid foundation in educational psychology, allowing
them to design and implement teaching practices that align with the
developmental and psychological needs of their students. They will be able
to assess and address a variety of learning challenges, fostering a
supportive and dynamic classroom environment
EDUC5500
Educational
Sociology
2
This course invites students to explore the dynamic relationship between
education and society through various theoretical perspectives,
emphasizing how education can both perpetuate and challenge social
inequalities. The objectives of the course include analyzing and applying
key educational theories, exploring how schools contribute to inequality
and stratification, and developing critical thinking skills to evaluate
educational practices and policies. Rooted in the belief that education is a
powerful tool for personal growth and societal change, the course
encourages active participation and critical engagement. Students will
engage in interactive discussions, mini-lectures, video clips, experiential
activities, and group exercises to bridge the gap between theory and
practice. By the end of the course, students will be able to critically analyze
educational theories, understand the impact of education on social mobility
and inequality, and apply their knowledge to real-world educational
settings. This course is designed for graduate students in
education__related fields, offering valuable insights into the intersection of
education and society.
EDUC5501
Professional
Ethics and Law
in Lebanese
Educational
System
3
This course delves into professional ethics and educational laws within the
Lebanese educational system. It equips educators with a thorough
understanding of their legal rights, responsibilities, and ethical obligations
through the study of Lebanese educational law, teachers' codes of conduct,
and ethical dilemmas in educational settings. Students will engage in
critical thinking, ethical decision-making, and practical applications of
educational policies, fostering a commitment to equitable and responsible
practices. The course employs a reflective, analytical approach, integrating
lectures, case studies, discussions, role-playing, and scenario analyses to
prepare educators for real-world challenges.
EDUC5502
Educational
Media and
Technology
3
How can educators harness the power of technology to transform learning
and engage students in meaningful ways__ This course delves into the
foundational and advanced aspects of integrating educational media and
technology into teaching. Students will explore a variety of tools and
platforms, from Google Apps and collaborative technologies to cutting-edge
artificial intelligence, to design dynamic and interactive learning
experiences. Through hands-on practice and collaborative projects,
students will learn to critically assess and selec_t appropriate technologies,
design technology-enhanced assessments, and create effective
instructional plans. Topics include technology integration models (TPACK,
SAMR), innovative tools for teaching and assessment, and current trends in
educational technology. By the end of the course, students will have
developed a mini-synthesis of research on educational technology and
gained practical experience in leveraging technology to meet diverse
learning needs. This course prepares educators to lead in the digital age,
equipping them with the skills and strategies needed to enhance
motivation, engagement, and efficacy in modern classrooms.
Major Requirements
Code
Title
Credits
Description
EDUC5070
Teaching
Economics I
3
This course is designed to provide instructors teaching economics at the
undergraduate level with the tools, techniques, and strategies necessary to
teach economics effectively. Teachers will explore a range of teaching
methods and best practices, with a focus on active learning strategies that
engage students in the learning process. The course will cover topics such as
lesson planning, assessment, course design, and pedagogical approaches that
are appropriate for different learning styles and levels of student ability. The
different objectives of this course will be reinforced through classroom
discussions, case studies, and authentic assessments. It includes discussions
of contemporary issues in economics education. Upon completion of the
course, instructors will be able to incorporate active learning and engage
students in the learning process.
EDUC5570
Teaching
Economics
II
3
Teaching Economics II builds on the foundational principles introduced in the
first course and emphasizes the practical application of teaching economics to
engage students in real-world, active learning experiences. The course is
designed to provide instructors with advanced strategies and methodologies
for teaching economics effectively, incorporating contemporary issues in
economics education, technology, and differentiated instruction to meet the
needs of diverse learners. Throughout this course, instructors will engage in
lesson planning, the use of authentic assessments, and curriculum design that
aligns with state and national standards for economics education. Active
learning, cooperative teaching, and ongoing reflection will be at the core of
the learning experience.
EDUC5571
Practicum of
Teaching
Economics
3
The Practicum of Teaching Economics course provides practical guidance for
economics instructors on course design, teaching methods, and assessment.
The course addresses some of the most common challenges that economics
instructors face, provides practical guidance on course design and delivery,
covers effective practices in assessment and evaluation, and explores
emerging trends in economics education. The course focuses on student-
centered learning and active engagement. Throughout the course, students
are provided with numerous examples and practices of how to incorporate
active learning and engage students in the learning process. This course
includes discussions of contemporary issues in economics education and
consists of field-based experience for enrolled students under the direct
supervision of a faculty mentor. Upon completion of the course, students are
provided with practical guidance and strategies for engaging students and
enhancing their learning experience.

EDUC5010
Teaching
Mathematics I
3
The course introduces prospective teachers to the essential principles,
methods, and practices of mathematics education. Designed for educators
beginning their journey in mathematics instruction, this course emphasizes
fundamental pedagogical approaches, effective communication of
mathematical concepts, and the development of strong mathematical
literacy among students. Students will explore core teaching methodologies,
examining how to build mathematical understanding through language-rich
environments, conceptual clarity, and operational mastery. Students will
learn to evaluate and implement educational resources, integrate
appropriate technology, and design assessments that effectively measure
student comprehension. Through interactive discussions, case study
analyses, and hands-on practice, students will develop their ability to create
engaging learning experiences. The course provides practical tools and
research-based strategies to help educators build students' confidence and
competence in mathematics. By the end of the course, students will be
prepared to create supportive learning environments that foster
mathematical thinking, encourage precise communication, and develop
students' problem-solving abilities through constructivist teaching
approaches.
EDUC5510
Teaching
Mathematics
II
3
Building on the foundational knowledge from Teaching of Mathematics I,
this course provides prospective teachers with a deeper understanding of
advanced mathematical topics and explores specialized pedagogical
techniques for teaching them. Designed for educators preparing to teach at
the high school level, this course emphasizes strategies for making abstract
mathematical ideas accessible, fostering mathematical reasoning, and
promoting advanced problem-solving skills. Students will delve into subjects
such as algebra, trigonometry, calculus, and discrete mathematics.,
examining innovative approaches to teaching these concepts. Students will
explore methods to integrate technology into your instruction, design
assessments to evaluate higher-order thinking, and adapt lessons to meet
the needs of diverse learners. Through hands-on activities, collaborative
lesson planning, and reflective practices, students will refine their ability to
design engaging and effective lessons. Practical tools and real-world
examples will support their efforts to inspire curiosity and confidence in
students tackling advanced mathematics. By the end of the course, students
will be equipped to create dynamic learning environments that empower
students to succeed in mathematics while fostering their critical thinking
and problem-solving abilities.
EDUC5511
Practicum of
Teaching
Mathematics
3
The Practicum of Teaching Mathematics is a critical component of a
Teaching Diploma program. It bridges theory and practice, allowing
students to apply pedagogical concepts and mathematical knowledge in real
classroom settings. This practicum aims to develop key teaching skills,
including lesson planning, classroom management, assessment, and the
ability to differentiate instruction for diverse learners. To ensure a
structured and effective practicum experience, training hours should be
distributed across various key areas, with a balance between observational
learning, direct teaching, feedback, and reflection.

The "Teaching of Fine Arts" course focuses on preparing future educators with
the essential pedagogical approaches, techniques, and understanding needed
to effectively teach fine arts in the classroom. The primary objective of this
course is to provide comprehensive instruction in various aspects of fine arts
education, such as teaching strategies, lesson planning, and assessment
methods, as well as foundational fine arts concepts like color, value, texture,
shape, line, and form. The course adheres to a philosophy that emphasizes
hands- on learning, practical application, and the development of strong
teaching skills in the context of fine arts education. For instance, students will
learn how to create engaging lesson plans that explore color theory, integrate
various art materials such as charcoal and clay, and foster creativity in their
students. The course will utilize a combination of lectures, demonstrations, and
hands-on activities, accompanied by regular assessments and feedback through
teaching practicum experiences, projects, and examinations. Upon successful
completion of the course, students will have demonstrated the ability to
effectively teach fine arts principles, create engaging and diverse lesson plans,
and evaluate and provide constructive feedback on student work.

teaching fine arts in educational settings. This course focuses on integrating
theoretical concepts with practical applications, exploring interdisciplinary
connections, and fostering a deeper understanding of fine arts pedagogy.
Students will develop the ability to create dynamic and inclusive fine arts
lessons, assess student growth in artistic skills, and utilize innovative teaching
strategies to inspire creativity and self-expression in learners. The course will
emphasize curriculum development, lesson planning, and strategies for
fostering critical and creative thinking in a range of fine arts disciplines,
including visual arts, sculpture, and mixed media.

themselves in the world of art, preparing them to teach fine arts effectively in a
Lebanese context through real-life teaching experience. This comprehensive
course aims to provide students with essential knowledge and skills for
teaching various forms of art, integrating art history, and applying art
education principles in the classroom. Rooted in the belief that art fosters
creativity and holistic learning, the course covers a diverse range of topics,
including teaching artistic behavior, fostering creativity, exploring the elements
and principles of art, and examining multicultural arts. Throughout the course,
students will engage in hands-on teaching practicum experiences in real
classroom settings, with opportunities to teach drawing, painting, mixed media,
ceramics, sculpture, and computer graphics. As part of the teaching
methodology, students will be required to complete practicum reports,
reflecting on their experiences and assessing their progress. These reports will
enable students to refine their teaching techniques and enhance their
understanding of art education. In addition, they will learn how to assess and
provide feedback to their students, integrating art into various subjects and
promoting a well-rounded educational experience. By the end of the course,
students will have developed the ability to design and implement engaging art
lessons, foster creativity in the classroom, and navigate the challenges of
teaching fine arts in a real-world context, supported by their practical
experiences and the insights gained from their practicum reports.

Bachelor of Communication Arts (Advertising)
Core Requirements
Code
Title
Credits
Description
ADVR300
Advertising Theory &
Practice
3
Advertising Theory and Practice provides a comprehensive overview on Advertising, its
role in building a brands image and brand equity, its diverse techniques used to
influence people's mind by satisfying or creating consumers needs, its communicational
impact on society that keeps on generating trends as well as its persuasive force in
increasing sales and encouraging consumers to make the purchase. Broad attention is
given to key subjects such as advertising agency practices, branding, media planning,
creative and marketing strategies.
ARTS350
Photography
3
Photography is addressed to all students who wish to learn about digital photography
basics, eventually, how to use a digital camera and lenses. Students will learn terms and
theory using manual techniques in a digital single lens reflex camera. This course
involves the power of images through image language, composition and philosophy. It
covers as well the use of the digital dark room for the enhancement of ideas, products
and /or creative necessity. It leads students towards a deeper understanding of light,
key value, equipment and camera controls
COMM200
Introduction to
Communication
Studies
3
Introduction to Mass Communication introduces students to the central concepts of
image theories in communication and the operation of the media industries. It is an
introduction to the history, structure, process and social environment of each medium in
the communication industry; an overview of the emerging technology in mass media and
its social impact. It is a study of the development, principles and effects of Print, Public
Relations, Advertising, Radio, TV, film and Computer/Online-Generated communication.
Particular attention will be given to the study of different types of mass and interactive
media and how they function in modern society. It reviews the historical and regulatory
bases of the media along with their social implications.
COMM220
Rhetoric & Persuasion
3
Rhetoric and Persuasion provides students with the foundation to understand the
definition of key terms, offering a retrospective glance to the historical foundations of
rhetoric and persuasion. It provides insights on important considerations of the
persuasion on the social through rhetoric. It provides a model for professional practice
focusing on developing skills in critical self-reflection, as well as professional
persuasion.
COMM225
Workshop
3
Workshop I is an entry-level course that will introduce students to the fundamentals of
video making. Students will learn to use video and sound as an effective form of
communication, and will learn how to successfully utilize those elements separately and
simultaneously, to be able to transform an idea into a persuasive story.
COMM265
Performance Theory &
Practice
3
Performance Theory and Practice introduces students to the ambiguity that lies in trying
to define what performance as a discipline might mean, which makes this course very
challenging. It is very essential to note that performance in not theatre, without
neglecting the fact that performing is a part of acting. The subject in action is not an
actor; he is only experiencing a new game where others, as subjects (physical and
emotional) are taking part in this game. What comes out of this game is what will
mark the journey of each and every subject involved in this class. It is not a theatre
course, but it involves character games, breathing techniques, mediation and a rough
body work. And because the discipline is still under construction all around the world,
the game is set between the students and the facilitator. Hence, the facilitator i.e.
the instructor is part of the game. It is all about a behavior in front of an audience.
COMM285
Theories of Perception
3
Theories of Perception is an introductory course on communication languages and
perception modes in relation to the technology of image production. It is an
investigation of the semiotics of representation and perception throughout different
medium usage and major art and media movements. It also covers the development of
image theories and representation toward the various elements of communication and
throughout history in relation to technology as a major variable for the image
production.
COMM305
Artificial Intelligence
and Mass Media
3
This course provides an in-depth exploration of the intersection between artificial
intelligence (AI) and mass media. It examines how AI technologies are transforming
media production, distribution, and consumption. Students will analyze the ethical
implications, the impact on journalism, advertising, and public relations, and the role of
AI in shaping societal narratives.
GDES270
Design Software I
3
Design software 1 introduces students to aiding software for Graphic Design. Using the
Adobe suite, Adobe Illustrator plays a significant role in graphic design. As a vector
oriented software, illustrator opens a gateway of opportunities for a graphic designer to
work with ease in implementing the essential work for print, web and other media.
Adobe InDesign complements Illustrator at producing multiple page content instead of
art boards and by that, playing an essential role at strengthening sense of layout and
identity. Adobe Photoshop plays a major role in photo editing. Accompanied by Adobe
illustrator, these 2 software manage to create most demanding projects especially that
of print. The student will have the opportunity to learn and practice the essentials in
these software. Keeping the sketchbook to bring up ideas to life, the designated
software shall add ease and speed rather than the long timed labor of manual work.
JORN285
Travel Journalism
3
Travel Journalism provides students with the foundation to understand the setting of the
fundamental writing skills required by freelance writers.  It exposes students to the
experience and savoir-faire of successful travel writing. Flexible in its approach, the
course teaches the craft of creating travel media through writing and photography,
covering diverse topics of journalism and blogging. The objective is to address markets
needs through building skills in the chosen medium and creating and marketing the
writers personal brand.
PREL300
Public Relations
Principles & Concepts
3
Public Relations Principles and Concept introduces students to the basic principles of
public relations. In this course, students will learn how to identify the main concepts
and principles in the field of public relations, which will further be elaborated on, in
subsequent courses. The course will also provide students with the knowledge to
practice the basics of PR
Major Requirements
Code
Title
Credits
Description
ADVR348
Advertising Pitching
3
Advertising Pitching is focused on the art and pitching process of an advertising agency
to a potential or existing client. The objective is to gain new businesses, to sell an idea
or product and/or to present the client with a new communication plan. Pitching is about
conveying and convincing.
ADVR350
Advertising
Copywriting
3
Advertising Copywriting is an introduction to the basic elements of writing for
advertising, focusing on concept creation and best practices for headlines, taglines and
slogans. All ad assignments are based on creative strategies developed by the students.
While English is the teaching language, Arabic slogans may be accepted depending on
the project and its requirements.
ADVR370
Psychology of
Advertising
3
The Psychology of Advertising course will study the theories of mass psychology and
human collective behaviors. It will emphasize the psychological impressions and styles
of advertising that carries the message to the consumers and caters to their emotions.
This class will also cover the most controversial and long-standing issues concerning
advertising and consumer socialization and the psychological effects of special selling
techniques.
ADVR390
Branding and
Corporate Identity
3
How do companies or people create compelling brand experiences? How
could you cultivate a well perceived brand? Branding and Corporate Identity is an
advanced design course with an emphasis on corporate brand identity development.
Topics include how to build a trustworthy brand, image and logo development,
marketing and advertising collateral, web branding, and broadcast advertising
development, all portraying the same brand message. Attention is given to the creation
of graphic standards.
ADVR410
Advertising & Sales
Promotion
3
In the Advertising and Sales Promotion course, students will learn how sales
promotions, one of the marketing tools of the promotional mix, are used to lift sales
temporarily, by appealing to economic motives and emotional impulse-buying behaviors,
determined by a careful Marketing Mix study.
Students will also learn how to apply and advertise the diverse short term techniques of
sales and promotion, aimed either at the consumer or at the distribution channel, in the
form of sales-incentives, to introduce new products, build brand awareness, attract
traffic and sales, create interest, and increase consumer demand.
Creativity and business are equally important aspects of sales promotion that must
follow a systematic planning approach to get the maximum value from their promotional
spending.
ADVR420
New Media in
advertising
3
New Media in Advertising helps students better understand the ever changing social
media landscapes, so to create effective consumer-targeted advertising campaigns. The
course will also teach students how strategize, plan and execute ads within the major
social channels to generate full funnel results across.
ADVR430
Advertising Storyboard
3
The Storyboard course is an advanced course about the creative process of
storyboarding for film in general and for creative advertising particularly. It is about
helping the students move the idea of the advertisement from concept, to script, to a
sequential visual story, by drawing the main scenes with the adequate image
composition. Students will explore the basic concepts of storyboarding by creating and
reviewing storyboards. The concepts addressed will include: tools, methods and
techniques, visual storytelling and narrative structure, shot composition, as well as
character development.
ADVR460
Advertising Creativity
3
Advertising Creativity is an advanced course about the creative process of advertising.
With the aim of broadening student knowledge and strengthening their background in
advertising creativity, students will be exposed to several documentaries related to
advertising creativity and many interviews of some important and successful figures of
the advertising industry. Students will also learn a series of methods and tools that will
aid them to move their creative ideas, to come up with successful advertising concepts
and to build creative advertising campaigns, that will communicate effectively the
benefit of the product/service to their audiences, using all types of media.
These creative methods will be backed with a collection of successful international ads
that will broaden the students creative spectrum and creative advertising knowledge.
ADVR485
Advertising Campaign
Design
3
Advertising Campaign Design introduces students to the application of Marketing and
Advertising principles and practices into the development of a Communication Strategy
and an Integrated Advertising Campaign. Students will learn to build a comprehensive
Advertising Strategy based on an efficient Marketing Mix and a creative marketable
vision that will lead to the development of a fully Integrated Advertising Campaign.
Multiple applications will be put to plan to serve a single unifying concept and diverse
tactics will be implemented, targeting specific audiences at specific timings. The
students will also team up to pitch a communication proposal for a client in an agency
style presentation.
ADVR495
Senior Study in
Advertising
3
Senior Study in Advertising is a marketplace experience with the processes of
fine-tuning a flood of ideas into a single advertising campaign pitch, and the translation
of ideas into advertising reality. In this class, students are exposed to top-ranking
creative professional visitors to present their philosophies, call for concepts and
critique, to determine which idea should be taken to the finish and how to research,
organize and write an advertising pitch. Senior students are exposed to the thinking of a
variety of executive-level professionals and have the opportunity to work with them.
Class continuity is maintained by a mentor who is present at all sessions to advice and
critique.
COMM300
Media Laws & Ethics
3
Media Laws and Ethics introduces students to the major legal, ethical and policy issues
related to the media. This course will expose students to primary documents and cases
as well as to methods of analysis. It will examine freedom of expression and the
limitations imposed on such freedoms by statue and by common Law, and will provide
students with the foundation necessary to make ethical decisions within their profession
focusing on developing analysis techniques and applying them to ethical problems
through independent critical thinking and moral sensitivity.
COMM310
Research Methods in
Communication Arts
3
Research Methods in Communication Arts introduces students to the essentials of
conducting a research dealing with communication as a social science. Students will
learn how to identify a problem, ask questions and find answers through systematic
procedures from a Social Science perspective.
COMM320
Radio-TV Announcing
3
Radio/TV Announcing establishes the foundations to understand types of news and
delivery techniques. It provides insights on important considerations for vocal ability.
The course will expose and guide students to the techniques of delivering news texts
when producing quality journalism. It will provide a model for professional anchoring
focusing on developing skills in reading news with a self-ability to discover and correct
errors in pronunciation.
COMM330
Media Planning &
Audience Analysis
3
Media Planning and Audience Analysis introduces students to the cooperate todays
landscape. Students will learn the social order instituted by modernity, the identity of
organizations and the messages being communicated both externally and internally.
Students will also learn the importance of audience demographics, psychographics, and
product usage variables, which help to make creative media decisions in tune with the
changing marketplace.
COMM400
Media Management
3
Media management introduces students to the business of media. It allows them to
explore the uniqueness of information as a product, shedding the light on two
perspective models, namely the market one and that of the public sphere. While the
market aims at profits and the public sphere is concerned with public interest, facts,
theories and articles related to these issues, are communicated to the students.
PREL455
Public Speaking
3
Public Speaking introduces students to the principles of public speaking; It critically
examines students own and others speeches through interactive practice. The course
introduces students to the essential of presentations, job interviews and in more general
instances of communication. It is an introduction to the rhetorical study dating back to
the Ancient Greeks, their structure and process of public speaking. It invites students to
critically examine their speeches as well as other students in addition to famous
speeches for formative purposes.
RATV316
Mobile Media
3
Mobile Media is an exploration of new video technologies involving digital photography
and portable video production, post-production and broadcast. It is a study of streaming
media for distribution on "hand- held" devices, "video casts" or "Podcast." Students from
Beirut Campus, Saida Campus, Nabatiyeh Campus and Tripoli Campus will all work
closely together in Beirut and another city of their choice to produce two video mapping
projects for each city.
RATV370
Writing for Radio and
TV
3
Writing for Radio and TV introduces students to the characteristics and rules for
effective writing for radio and TV while focusing on writing for simple news and reports.
The course teaches students the best ways to write for the ear in the case of writing for
radio, while focusing on the two levels that characterize such writing: Voice Over and
Natural Sound. As for writing for TV, it gives guidelines on how to write for the eye and
